Full-Service Bathroom Remodeling Solutions in Sacramento

We provide complete bathroom remodeling services designed to improve comfort, functionality, and long-term durability. From small upgrades to full renovations, our team focuses on high-quality craftsmanship and designs that fit the needs of Sacramento homeowners.

Whether you want a modern walk-in shower, a complete master bathroom remodel, or custom tile flooring, we handle every step of the remodeling process — from planning and demolition to installation and final inspection.

Our Sacramento bathroom remodeling services include:

Tub-to-Shower Conversions

Many homeowners are replacing traditional bathtubs with modern showers to create more space and improve accessibility. A tub-to-shower conversion can make your bathroom feel larger, brighter, and easier to maintain.

Our conversions are designed to maximize both functionality and style while ensuring long-term waterproof protection.

Homeowners who want a more modern and open bathroom often choose our Tub to Shower Conversion Services in Sacramento.

Features can include:

• Slip-resistant shower flooring
• Built-in shelving and storage niches
• Frameless glass shower doors
• Durable waterproof wall panels

This upgrade is one of the most effective ways to modernize an outdated bathroom while improving everyday convenience.

Walk-In Shower Installation

Walk-in showers are one of the most popular bathroom remodeling upgrades in Sacramento. They offer a clean, modern design while making the space easier to use and maintain.

Our team specializes in installing custom showers that fit the exact layout of your bathroom.

Many Sacramento homeowners upgrade their bathrooms with our Walk-In Shower Installation Services to create a more spacious and accessible shower area.

Our walk-in showers can include:

• Frameless glass enclosures for an open look
• Built-in seating for added comfort
• Multiple showerhead options such as rain or handheld showers
• Custom tile designs and wall panels

Walk-in showers are ideal for homeowners who want a modern design combined with long-term durability.

Bathtub Replacement

If your bathtub is outdated, damaged, or difficult to clean, replacing it can dramatically improve the appearance and functionality of your bathroom.

Our team installs high-quality bathtubs designed for durability and comfort.

Homeowners looking to upgrade their existing tub often choose our Bathtub Replacement Services in Sacramento for a fast and professional installation.

Our bathtub options include:

• Durable acrylic and solid-surface tubs
• Deep soaking tubs for relaxation
• Space-saving alcove bathtub designs
• Matching surrounds and updated fixtures

A new bathtub can refresh the entire look of your bathroom while improving everyday comfort.

Small Bathroom Remodeling

Small bathrooms can still feel spacious and functional with the right design strategy. Our remodeling approach focuses on maximizing storage, improving layout, and selecting materials that make the room feel larger.

If you want to improve a compact bathroom, explore our Small Bathroom Remodeling Services in Sacramento.

We help homeowners achieve better space efficiency through:

• Space-saving vanity designs
• Walk-in shower upgrades
• Light-enhancing tile selections
• Smart storage solutions

Even small remodeling upgrades can significantly improve the comfort and usability of your bathroom.

Master Bathroom Remodeling

A master bathroom remodel allows homeowners to transform their bathroom into a relaxing and functional space that matches the rest of their home.

Our team works closely with homeowners to design custom layouts and premium finishes.

For a complete bathroom transformation, many homeowners choose our Master Bathroom Remodeling Services in Sacramento.

Master bathroom upgrades may include:

• Large walk-in showers
• Double vanity installations
• Luxury tile flooring
• Modern lighting and mirror upgrades

A master bathroom remodel can add both comfort and long-term value to your home.

Custom Tile & Flooring Installation

Tile and flooring play a major role in the appearance and durability of any bathroom remodel. High-quality tile not only improves the design but also protects the bathroom from moisture damage.

We install custom tile layouts designed to complement your entire bathroom renovation.

If you're planning a bathroom upgrade, our Custom Tile and Flooring Installation Services in Sacramento can help create a beautiful and durable foundation for your space.

Our tile installation services include:

• Porcelain and ceramic tile flooring
• Shower wall tile designs
• Slip-resistant bathroom flooring
• Custom tile patterns and layouts

Well-installed tile adds lasting durability while giving your bathroom a polished, high-end appearance.

Kitchen Remodeling in Sacramento California
THRIVE HOME CONSTRUCTION
Our Specialty: Kitchen Remodels

We'll turn your kitchen into the design you've always pictured, backed by our 3-year warranty. At Thrive Home Construction, we don't cut corners, we build it right.

We specialize in creating stunning, functional spaces tailored to your home.
Kitchen Remodeling: From full layout overhauls to modern refreshes, we handle every detail with precision. We transform the heart of your Sacramento home with expert craftsmanship.

Confidence Built-In: Every project is backed by our installation workmanship coverage.

The Thrive Difference: Our 3 Guarantees
3-Year Warranty: We offer a 3-year warranty with no questions asked because we stand behind our workmanship.

On-Time Promise: We value your time. If we are late on your project, we will refund you $100 for each delayed day.

Dust-Free & Clean: We protect your home like it’s our own. We use sealed work zones, dust control, and daily cleanup to ensure an organized environment.

Enjoy Your New Kitchen Transformation

Choosing a new kitchen is exciting, but the process can feel overwhelming. Deciding on materials, planning the right layout, and managing the disruption to daily life can add stress to what should be a rewarding upgrade. Thrive Home Construction removes that uncertainty with a predictable, stress-free experience from first consultation to final walkthrough.

Our kitchen remodeling process is built around clear communication, a firm project timeline, and lasting results. Every job is backed by our 3-Year Workmanship Warranty and our On-Time Promise, so you know exactly what to expect and when to expect it.

 

Custom Kitchen Solutions for Sacramento & Beyond

 

Thrive Home Construction brings a full range of kitchen options to fit your vision and your home. From custom cabinetry and quartz or granite countertops to islands, backsplash tile, and full layout redesigns, we tailor every detail to how you actually live and cook.

No two kitchens are the same, which is why we start every project with a free design consultation. We walk through your space, talk through how you use it day to day, and put together a plan that fits your style and your budget before any work begins. You get a clear, upfront quote so there are no surprises once the project starts.

Your Kitchen, Built the Right Way

We keep the process simple so you always know what comes next. It starts with a free design consultation, followed by a clear plan and a firm quote, then a clean, on-time build backed by our guarantees. No guesswork, no hidden steps, just a straightforward path to the kitchen you want.

Once the design is finalized, our team handles every phase of the build so you are not coordinating separate contractors for cabinetry, countertops, tile, and electrical. One point of contact, one schedule, and one team accountable for the results from demo day to final walkthrough.

 

Why Sacramento Homeowners Choose Thrive

 

Every kitchen we build comes with the same promises. A 3-Year Workmanship Warranty backing every detail, an On-Time Promise that puts real money behind our schedule, and a sealed, dust-free work zone so your home stays livable while we work. It is the same standard we have built our reputation on, now applied to your kitchen.

These are not just promises we make and hope to keep. Our On-Time Promise pays you directly if we fall behind, and our 3-Year Warranty means we stand behind the work long after the project is finished. It is a level of accountability most contractors will not put in writing.

ABOUT THRIVE HOME CONSTRUCTION
Local Luxury Kitchen Remodelers In Sacramento, California: Elevate Your Home's Comfort

Founded by Andrey Tsushko, a passionate home renovator and proud father of six, Thrive was created to serve homeowners who value quality, trust, and results. Our mission is to ensure your home feels protected and elevated at every stage of the renovation.

Transform your kitchen into a space you love with our expert remodeling and renovation services. From custom cabinetry to functional layouts, we tailor each project to your unique style and needs, ensuring a space that not only looks stunning but also enhances your home's value.

For homeowners across the Greater Sacramento region, we deliver bathroom remodels that combine expert workmanship, clear communication, and a seamless, stress-free experience from start to finish.

Built on integrity and fueled by a passion for transforming homes, Thrive has become a trusted name for homeowners who want high-end results without the hassle, hidden fees, or runaround that many contractors are known for.

Hi, I'm Andrey Tsushko, founder of Thrive Home Construction, a family-owned bathroom remodeling company specializing in durable, stylish designs for busy households.

As parents of six homeschooled kids, my wife and I understand the chaos of family life. Our home endures constant heavy use—from slammed doors and endless showers to creative "experiments" that test every fixture. We've replaced cheap materials too many times, so we built our business around bathrooms that last.
Why Choose Our Family-Owned Bathroom Services?

Durable Materials: Easy-to-clean surfaces and sturdy hardware built for kids and heavy traffic.
Stylish & Thoughtful Designs: We partner with professional designers to create spaces that are not only tough but also beautifully modern and customized for your home.
Personal Expertise: As a homeschool family, we know what works for high-use, high-style bathrooms.

We're not just remodelers—we create durable and stylish bathrooms that handle your family's daily adventures while elevating your home's aesthetic.
Join our family of satisfied customers. Contact us today!

💬 “We don’t just build bathrooms — we create spaces where people feel at home.”

Our Mission

To elevate the homes and lifestyles of Sacramento-area families by delivering high-quality, dependable, and beautifully executed bathroom renovations — on time and on budget.

Our Philosophy

We don't cut corners, we build smarter, faster, and better.

We believe that a remodel should not be a disruptive, messy, or chaotic process. It should be an exciting journey that culminates in an elevated living space. Our approach is built on three core pillars:

Quality Craftsmanship

We ensure lasting, high-quality results in every installation. Every project is completed with precision, durable materials, and industry-leading standards. We don’t cut corners — we build bathrooms that perform and look great for the long run.

Protection

We treat your home like it's our own, utilizing sealed work zones and rigorous dust control.

Dependability

We stand by our On-Time Promise and dependable scheduling.

BUILT ON QUALITY AND TRUST
Why Sacramento Homeowners Choose Thrive
Reliable Communication
We keep you updated — no guessing, no disappearing contractors.
Professional Team
Skilled builders, installers, and designers dedicated to quality.
Licensed & Insured
Your home is in safe, qualified hands.
Respect for Your Space
We protect your home, minimize disruption, and clean thoroughly after every workday.
Results You’ll Love
Your bathroom isn’t done until you’re fully satisfied.
THRIVE HOME CONSTRUCTION
Our Promise to You

When you choose Thrive Home Construction, you're choosing a team that treats your home like our own. We’re committed to delivering results that not only improve your bathroom — but improve your everyday life.

We also back our projects with a comprehensive warranty. If something isn't right with the installation workmanship across your remodel, we make it right—fast, fair, and hassle-free, giving you peace of mind long after the final walkthrough.

We remodel with care.
We build with integrity.
And we always stand behind our work.

About ARIID Build & Remodel

Est. 2006  |  BBB Accredited — A+ Rated  |  NKBA Member  |  As Featured In: 425 Magazine · City Lifestyle · Globe Newswire

Get to know ARIID Build & Remodel: Your trusted partner for home transformations in Kirkland, Bellevue, Mercer Island, Issaquah, and more.

WHO WE ARE

At ARIID Build & Remodel, we pride ourselves on being industry leaders in home remodeling and construction. Founded by Ariana, a professional with decades of experience in the construction sector, ARIID Build & Remodel combines innovative design with expert craftsmanship. Ariana also leads Ariana Designs & Interiors, bringing a visionary approach to every project we undertake.

Our Journey

Ariid Build & Remodel began as the natural extension of our design work. We saw too many projects lose their magic between the drawing board and the job site, so we created a construction company with one mission: to protect the vision and deliver craftsmanship you can trust.

Our Why

We do this work because building isn’t just construction—it’s creation. It’s the moment when ideas become reality, when families finally see their dreams take shape. Our purpose is to make the building process smoother, more transparent, and more rewarding for our clients.

Our Difference

What sets Ariid Build apart is integration. Most builders build; we build with design at the forefront. As part of the Ariid Group, we collaborate closely with designers, ensuring that every finish, detail, and proportion honors the original vision. This unity between design and construction is rare—and it’s why our clients trust us to bring their most important projects to life.

Our Commitment to Quality

At ARIID Build & Remodel, we handpick our award-winning designers and trusted subcontractors for their professionalism, skill, and meticulous attention to detail. This collaboration ensures we deliver top-tier results, creating beautiful, functional, and long-lasting spaces that exceed our clients’ expectations. We believe that the key to every successful project lies in the seamless collaboration between our talented team and skilled subcontractors, all dedicated to bringing your vision to life.

Client-Centric Approach

At ARIID Build & Remodel, we prioritize strong client relationships and open communication throughout every stage of the remodeling process. Understanding that your home reflects your style and needs, we work diligently to fully realize your vision. Our team keeps you informed with regular updates and transparent communication, ensuring a smooth and enjoyable experience from consultation to completion. Your satisfaction is our top priority, and we strive to deliver exceptional craftsmanship that stands the test of time.

Serving the Greater Seattle Area

ARIID Build & Remodel proudly serves the greater Seattle area, including Kirkland, Bellevue, Mercer Island, Redmond, Issaquah, and surrounding communities. We are dedicated to transforming your space with expertise, precision, and a passion for excellence.

MEET THE TEAM

ARIANA ADIREH ANDERSON

CEO / HEAD OF DESIGN

Ariana, founder of Ariid Build and Remodel, brings over 20 years of expertise in the industry. Her experience at Ariana Designs & Interiors has allowed her to consistently deliver innovative, high-quality construction and design solutions.

NICK ANDERSON

PRESIDENT

Nick contributes extensive leadership and operational expertise to Ariid Build and Remodel, focusing on delivering exceptional craftsmanship and innovative solutions for residential and commercial projects.

ISABEL VALENTA

DESIGN-BUILD PROJECT MANAGER

Isabel helps guide projects from the initial consultation through final installation, coordinating every stage of the process with our design, construction, and furnishings teams. Through site visits, subcontractor coordination, and quality oversight, she helps ensure each project is completed according to the approved plans while delivering a seamless experience for our clients.

ALEX EVANSON

CONTROLLER

Alex Evanson manages ARIID Build & Remodel’s financial operations and accounting. He ensures sound fiscal planning and reporting across all company projects.

 LINE BEAUDETTE

CUSTOMER CONCIERGE

Line is often the first point of contact for our clients, helping guide them through every stage of their project with warmth, organization, and attention to detail. With a background in hospitality and residential property management, she coordinates communication, scheduling, and client support to ensure a seamless experience from the initial consultation through project completion.

WHAT IT’S LIKE TO WORK WITH US

Who We Serve

Our clients are homeowners who want more than a contractor. They’re families expanding into their forever homes, individuals reimagining outdated spaces, or couples investing in a ground-up build. They come to us because they want peace of mind and the assurance that every detail will be handled with care.

The Transformation

Many clients start out overwhelmed by the complexity of building—permits, contractors, materials, and timelines. By the time we’re finished, they walk into a home that feels flawless, as though it always belonged to them. Instead of stress, they’re left with pride and joy in a space built to last.

At ARIID Build & Remodel, we believe in creating a positive experience for our clients. From the initial consultation through to project completion, we work collaboratively with you to bring your home transformation dreams to life.

Hear from our client, Mark S.

AWARDS

ARIID Build & Remodel has earned recognition across the Pacific Northwest for design excellence, craftsmanship, and client experience. Our team has been honored by clients and peers alike for delivering exceptional design-build projects — from luxury kitchen and bathroom remodels to custom new construction — across Kirkland, Bellevue, Sammamish, and the greater Seattle Eastside.

Meet the team behind the work. ARIID Build & Remodel offers fully integrated design and construction services across Kirkland, Bellevue, and the greater Seattle Eastside — from your first conversation through final completion.

Custom Home Building on the Eastside — Architecture, Permits, and Construction Under One Roof

The greatest risk in building a custom home is not the construction itself — it is the gap between what your architect designed and what your builder can actually deliver on time and on budget. The traditional architect-plus-general-contractor model separates the people who make design decisions from the people who manage construction costs and schedules. That gap is where most custom home projects go over budget, run over schedule, or arrive at a finished product that differs from what was originally designed. ARIID eliminates that gap entirely: our architecture and design team and our construction team are the same organization.

ARIID’s design-build new construction process runs as one continuous workflow: site analysis and feasibility, schematic design, design development, construction documents and permit submittal, construction management, and certificate of occupancy — all under one contract, with one project manager, and one team accountable for every decision. The design is calibrated to the budget from day one because the designers and builders are the same people. There are no surprises when the GC prices the architect’s drawings, because the GC is the architect.

New construction permits are the most complex permit process in residential work. A custom home in Kirkland or Bellevue requires full architectural and structural drawings, energy code compliance documentation (Washington State Energy Code is among the most demanding in the country), civil engineering on many sites, stormwater management plans, and inspections at foundation, framing, rough mechanical, and multiple finish phases. ARIID prepares every component of the permit package, manages all plan review correspondence with the applicable jurisdiction, and schedules every required inspection.

The Eastside new construction context shapes how ARIID approaches each project. Infill lots in Kirkland and Bellevue are constrained by setbacks, height limits, and lot coverage maximums that require precise site planning from the first schematic sketch. Teardown-rebuild projects on established lots bring their own site conditions — existing utilities, mature trees subject to retention requirements, and neighbors who are accustomed to a certain neighborhood character. Vacant land in communities like Yarrow Point, Clyde Hill, and Mercer Island carries estate-scale expectations for both the home and the design process.

Every ARIID custom home is designed from the site conditions, client program, and specific neighborhood character outward — not from a stock plan adapted to the site. The result is a home that belongs where it is built: that takes advantage of its specific views, light, and landscape, is calibrated to the street and neighborhood it occupies, and is built to current code and current thermal performance standards with the same luxury material tier we apply to our remodeling work. Our NKBA award recognition and BBB A+ rating are the professional credentials that back that standard.

Frequently Asked Questions About Custom Home Building

What does design-build mean for new home construction?
In a design-build new construction project, your architecture and design team and your general contractor are the same organization. ARIID handles site analysis, architectural design, engineering coordination, permit submission, and construction under one contract with one project manager. This eliminates the most common failure point in custom home projects — design decisions made without full awareness of construction cost and schedule implications. At ARIID, the design is calibrated to the budget from day one because the designers and builders are the same team.

What types of custom home projects does ARIID Build handle?
ARIID builds custom homes on infill lots in Kirkland and Bellevue, teardown-rebuild projects on established Eastside lots, and new construction on vacant land throughout King County. We work with homeowners building their long-term primary residence, investment properties, and estate-scale homes in communities like Yarrow Point, Clyde Hill, and Mercer Island. Every project is designed from the site and client program outward — we do not work from stock plans.

How long does a design-build custom home take from start to finish?
A design-build custom home on the Eastside typically takes 14 to 20 months from initial design kick-off to certificate of occupancy. Design and permitting run 4 to 6 months depending on project complexity and jurisdiction. Construction typically runs 10 to 14 months depending on square footage, site conditions, and finish level. Kitchen Remodeling on the Seattle Eastside — Design, Permits, and Construction Under One Roof

The most common failure mode in kitchen remodeling is not the work itself — it is scope defined in isolation from the realities of the existing structure. A kitchen in a split-level Bellevue home has different structural constraints than a single-level home in Kirkland. A client who wants to relocate a wall requires structural engineering before design drawings commit to anything. When these realities are discovered mid-project, schedules slip and budgets inflate.

ARIID’s design-build kitchen remodeling process addresses this by running design and construction as one integrated team. Our designers produce drawings calibrated to your existing structure, utility locations, and the lead times of the materials we specify. By the time we submit for permit and begin demolition, every decision has been made against the constraints that will actually govern construction. There are no change orders driven by surprises in the walls, because the contractor and designer investigated those conditions together before finalizing the design.

Kitchen permits in Kirkland, Bellevue, and surrounding Eastside jurisdictions require drawings for any work involving structural changes, electrical panel upgrades, ventilation penetrations, or plumbing relocations. ARIID prepares every required permit document, manages plan review correspondence, and schedules all required inspections. The permit process does not surprise our clients because we anticipate what each jurisdiction requires before the package is submitted.

The Eastside kitchen remodel market reflects the homes it serves — larger square footages, higher finish expectations, and clients investing in the primary space where they live and entertain. Most of our kitchen clients are upgrading cabinetry and countertops, reconfiguring layout to improve flow, improving lighting and ventilation, and selecting appliances at the same tier our sister company ARIID Home & Furniture sources for its furnishings clients. Our NKBA award recognition and BBB A+ rating reflect the standard we maintain on every project.

Frequently Asked Questions About Kitchen Remodeling

What does a kitchen remodel cost in Kirkland or Bellevue?
A full kitchen remodel on the Eastside typically ranges from $65,000 to $175,000+ depending on square footage, layout changes, structural work, and finish level. Mid-range updates with standard layout and refreshed finishes run $65,000–$95,000. Major transformations with layout reconfiguration, custom cabinetry, and premium appliances typically run $120,000–$200,000. ARIID provides detailed cost estimates after an initial site visit assessing existing conditions, client program, and material tier.

How long does a kitchen remodel take from start to finish?
A kitchen remodel with ARIID typically runs 3 to 5 months from design kick-off to final walkthrough. Design and permitting take 4 to 6 weeks for standard scopes; kitchens with structural changes take longer. Construction typically runs 6 to 10 weeks. Custom cabinetry has lead times of 8 to 12 weeks and governs the construction schedule — ARIID builds this into the project timeline at kick-off.

Do I need a permit to remodel a kitchen in Kirkland or Bellevue?
Yes, remodels involving electrical work, plumbing relocation, structural changes, or new ventilation penetrations require building permits. A cosmetic update — new countertops, cabinet refinishing, appliance swaps — typically does not. ARIID evaluates permit requirements at the initial project assessment and manages the entire process as part of our design-build scope.

The most expensive bathroom remodels are rarely the ones that cost the most at contract signing — they are the ones where undiscovered conditions during demolition require design changes mid-construction. At ARIID, the people who design your bathroom and the people who build it are the same team, so these conditions are anticipated before the design is committed — not discovered after demolition.

ARIID’s bathroom remodeling process begins with a condition assessment that identifies the actual state of the framing, waterproofing, and mechanical rough-ins before design drawings are finalized. Structural conditions, water damage, outdated plumbing, and substandard ventilation are all addressed in the design — not in a change order. The result is a project where the design you approved is the bathroom you receive, built within the budget and schedule you set at project kick-off.

Bathroom permits on the Eastside are required for any work involving plumbing rough-in changes, ventilation modifications, electrical work beyond fixture replacement, or structural modifications. ARIID manages the complete permit process — drawings, submittal, plan review correspondence, and inspection scheduling — as part of our scope. Clients are never left managing a permit process they did not expect.

The Eastside bathroom remodel client is investing in a space used every day. Home Remodeling on the Seattle Eastside — Why Integrated Design and Construction Matters

Whole-home and major scope remodeling projects fail more predictably than smaller projects, not because the work is harder, but because the coordination demands are higher. When a kitchen remodel, primary bathroom, and main floor reconfiguration are running simultaneously, every subcontractor’s schedule depends on the one before them. A two-week delay in cabinet delivery cascades into a three-week slip in countertop templating and a four-week slip in final electrical and plumbing trim-out. Without a design-build team managing these dependencies from a single plan, the schedule becomes a series of reactive adjustments rather than a managed sequence.

ARIID’s whole-home remodeling process runs on a single integrated project schedule built from the design phase forward. Before construction begins, we have ordered all long-lead materials, confirmed subcontractor availability, and established the critical path. Our project managers track that critical path in real time throughout construction — not by reacting to problems, but by managing the conditions that prevent problems from occurring. The design team and construction team share the same project management system, so a finish change in design does not arrive at the job site as a surprise.

Major home remodels in Kirkland and Bellevue often involve structural engineering, energy code compliance upgrades, and permits across multiple trades. A project that reconfigures the main floor, updates the mechanical system, and adds a deck requires building, mechanical, and potentially stormwater permits. ARIID prepares every permit application, manages all plan review correspondence, and schedules every required inspection — across all permit types — as part of our scope. Clients are not left managing a permit process they did not anticipate.

The Eastside whole-home remodel client is typically investing in their long-term primary residence and wants the result to hold up for decades — not just aesthetically but structurally, mechanically, and in terms of energy performance. ARIID designs to current energy code, selects materials with established durability records in the Pacific Northwest climate, and coordinates closely with ARIID Home & Furniture on furnishings so the architecture and the interior are coherent from the first day you move back in. Our NKBA award recognition and BBB A+ rating reflect the standard we bring to every project, regardless of scope.

How much does a major home remodel cost in Kirkland or Bellevue?
A major whole-home or multi-room remodel on the Eastside typically ranges from $150,000 to $500,000+ depending on scope, structural work, finish level, and square footage. Projects involving full kitchen and primary bathroom remodels plus main floor reconfiguration typically run $200,000–$350,000. ARIID provides detailed project cost estimates after a full site walk and program meeting.

How long does a major home remodel take?
A major home remodel with ARIID typically runs 5 to 10 months from design kick-off to final walkthrough depending on scope. Construction on a full kitchen plus primary bathroom plus main floor remodel typically runs 4 to 6 months. ARIID builds a full project schedule at kick-off so clients know the sequence before demo begins.

Do I need to move out during a major home remodel?
It depends on the scope. Projects that involve full kitchen and primary bathroom demo simultaneously usually require clients to live elsewhere for 6 to 10 weeks. ARIID discusses relocation planning with every client at project kick-off and designs the construction sequence to minimize the period when the home is uninhabitable.

Home Additions on the Seattle Eastside — Expanding Your Home Without Starting Over

A home addition is architecturally the most demanding residential project type: it must connect new construction to an existing structure seamlessly, match the original home’s character while meeting current code requirements, and deliver added square footage that functions as a natural extension of the original floor plan. The challenges are not just aesthetic. A second-story addition over an existing foundation requires structural evaluation of what the foundation can actually carry. A rear addition that crosses a setback line requires a variance process before design can be finalized. An addition that adds a bedroom requires code-compliant egress, ventilation, and electrical load capacity that the existing systems may not support.

ARIID’s home addition process begins with a feasibility assessment that identifies these constraints before design begins. We evaluate the existing structure’s capacity, the applicable setback and zoning requirements, and the condition of the systems the addition will connect to. Design is not committed until we understand what the existing home can support, what the jurisdiction will permit, and what the structural engineering requires. The result is a design that is buildable as drawn — not a design that needs to be revised when construction realities emerge.

Home addition permits on the Eastside are among the more complex residential permit applications. A second-story addition requires full architectural and structural drawings, energy code compliance documentation for the new envelope, and potentially geotechnical review if the addition changes the load distribution significantly. ARIID manages the complete permit process — all drawings, submittal, plan review correspondence, and inspection scheduling — within our scope. Clients are not managing a permit process they did not expect.

The Eastside home addition client is typically choosing to expand rather than move: they want to stay in a neighborhood they know, keep children in schools they have chosen, and add the square footage their household needs without the transaction costs of selling and buying. ARIID designs additions that match the original material palette, roofline character, and proportional vocabulary of the existing structure — additions that a neighbor or a future buyer would not identify as additions at all. Our BBB A+ accreditation and NKBA recognition back the quality standard we bring to this work.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a home addition cost in Kirkland or Bellevue?
A home addition on the Eastside typically runs $350 to $600 per square foot for the addition itself, depending on scope, finish level, and structural complexity. A 400-square-foot primary suite addition typically costs $140,000–$240,000. A second-story addition of 800 square feet typically runs $280,000–$480,000, plus any structural reinforcement the existing foundation requires. ARIID provides detailed cost estimates after a site visit that assesses existing conditions and structural capacity.

How long does a home addition take from start to finish?
A home addition with ARIID typically runs 6 to 12 months from design kick-off to completion depending on scope and structural complexity. Design and permitting take 6 to 10 weeks for straightforward additions; second-story additions with structural and geotechnical review take longer. Construction typically runs 3 to 5 months. ARIID builds the complete project schedule at kick-off so clients understand the full timeline before committing to design.

Will a home addition add value to my home in Kirkland or Bellevue?
Yes, well-designed home additions in the Kirkland-Bellevue market consistently add value exceeding their construction cost, particularly additions that add a primary suite, home office, or usable living space that the original floor plan lacked. The key factors are design quality — the addition must read as part of the original home architecturally — and finish level appropriate to the neighborhood. ARIID designs every addition to match the character and quality tier of the existing home and the surrounding neighborhood.

Aging in Place Remodeling on the Seattle Eastside — Building for the Long Term

Aging in place remodeling is the least understood category of residential work and, for the right client, the most valuable investment they can make in their home. The goal is not to make a home look like a medical facility — it is to design and build modifications that allow a homeowner to live safely and comfortably in their home for decades, regardless of how their mobility or physical capacity changes over time. Done well, aging in place remodeling is invisible: grab bars that read as elegant towel bars, curbless showers that look like luxury spa decisions, widened doorways that appear as architectural choices rather than accessibility accommodations.

ARIID’s aging in place remodeling process begins with a detailed assessment of the home and the client’s specific program. Not every client needs the same modifications — a client preparing for a planned joint surgery has different short-term needs than a client planning a 20-year horizon in a home they intend never to leave. We work with clients to identify the modifications that will have the greatest functional impact, prioritize them by urgency and complexity, and build a scope that achieves the client’s long-term goals without unnecessary work.

The structural and permit dimensions of aging in place work are often underestimated. Doorway widening to ADA-compliant 36 inches requires header work in most load-bearing walls — it is structural remodeling, not cosmetic carpentry. Zero-threshold shower installations require subfloor modification to create the proper drain slope. Grab bar installation in tile must anchor to blocking in the wall behind the tile, which means knowing where the blocking is before tile is set. ARIID plans every one of these elements in the design phase so the work is executed correctly the first time, with the proper permits where required.

Many of ARIID’s aging in place clients are also ARIID Home & Furniture clients — they want their home modifications to be beautiful as well as functional, and they want the finish selections to integrate with the furnishings and design character of the home as a whole. An aging in place bathroom can have the same tile quality, the same frameless glass, and the same lighting design as a primary suite renovation — it simply has a curbless threshold, blocking behind the tile for future grab bars, and a layout that accommodates a wheelchair or walker if needed. Our NKBA award recognition and BBB A+ accreditation are the professional credentials that back the standard we hold on every project.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does aging in place remodeling typically cost in Kirkland or Bellevue?
Aging in place modifications range widely depending on scope. A bathroom conversion with curbless shower, grab bars, and ADA-height fixtures typically runs $35,000–$75,000 on the Eastside. A whole-home aging in place assessment with bathroom conversion, doorway widening, and main-floor bedroom addition or conversion typically runs $80,000–$200,000+. ARIID provides detailed cost estimates after a site walk and program discussion to understand which modifications will have the greatest long-term value for your specific household.

Do aging in place modifications require permits?
Some do and some do not. Structural work — doorway widening, subfloor modification for zero-threshold showers, wall modifications to install blocking — requires building permits. Grab bar installation in existing tile does not. ARIID evaluates permit requirements at the initial project meeting and manages all required permits within our design-build scope.

Can aging in place modifications be done in phases?
Yes, and ARIID often recommends a phased approach. Phase one typically addresses the modifications with the greatest immediate safety impact — the primary bathroom, the main entry, and any significant fall hazards. Phase two may address doorway widening, kitchen modifications, or an ADU or main-floor bedroom addition for future single-level living. Planning the full scope upfront — even if execution is phased — ensures that phase one work is compatible with phase two without unnecessary demo or rework.

Design-Build Home Remodeling in Bellevue, WA

Bellevue is one of the Pacific Northwest’s most sought-after cities, and its homes reflect that ambition. Whether it’s a West Bellevue estate needing a kitchen upgrade, a Somerset home seeking more space, or a Downtown condo ready for transformation, ARIID Build & Remodel brings the design sophistication and construction precision to deliver exceptional results. Our design-build team manages every detail under one roof, ensuring your remodel is thoughtfully designed, precisely built, and truly worth the investment.

Home Remodeling Bellevue

A home remodel in Bellevue is a meaningful investment—and it deserves a contractor who treats it that way. At ARIID Build & Remodel, our home remodeling services are built around a simple principle: your home should work as well as it looks, and look as good as the neighborhood it belongs to. Bellevue homeowners have high expectations—for their finishes, their layouts, their project experience, and the team they trust to deliver. We meet every one of those expectations by keeping design and construction integrated from the very first conversation through the final walkthrough. One team. One vision. One outcome you can be genuinely proud of.

What Design-Build Means for a Bellevue Remodel

Most Bellevue remodels fail at the seams — the handoff between the person who drew the plans and the crew who has to build them. Design-build removes that handoff. ARIID Build & Remodel holds a single contract covering design, engineering, permitting, and construction, so one team is accountable from the first measurement to the final walkthrough. There is no second bid after the drawings are finished, and no argument about whether a problem is a design error or a field error.

One contract, one budget, one schedule

In a traditional design-bid-build arrangement you hire a designer, wait for drawings, then take those drawings to market and discover what they actually cost. On a Bellevue project that gap routinely adds two to four months and a redesign cycle when the bids come back over budget. Our estimators price the work while it is still being drawn, which means the scope is reconciled against a real number before you sign, not after.

Permits handled in-house through Bellevue Development Services

Bellevue reviews residential work more closely than most Eastside jurisdictions, and structural changes, additions, and anything touching a critical area or steep slope get scrutiny. Seattle Home Remodeling Starts With a Permit Question. Most Projects Underestimate How Long the Answer Takes.

Seattle’s Department of Construction and Inspections (SDCI) is one of the highest-volume permit offices in the Pacific Northwest, serving a city that is simultaneously adding density, preserving historic neighborhoods, and managing one of the most active renovation markets on the West Coast. The result is a permit timeline that is the single largest schedule variable on any Seattle home remodeling project — and the one that most homeowners and general contractors do not plan for adequately.

Simple residential alterations that qualify for over-the-counter review can move in 4 to 10 weeks. Projects with structural changes, additions, ADU conversions, or homes in designated historic districts require full plan review — and during peak SDCI volume, that process runs 10 to 20 weeks or longer. ARIID Build submits at the earliest qualified design stage, manages the SDCI portal through every review cycle, and uses the review window productively: material selection, subcontractor scheduling, and procurement of long-lead items happen while the permit is in queue, not after it is issued.

Pre-1980 Seattle homes require asbestos survey and abatement for any renovation touching materials installed before that date — a Washington State requirement that applies broadly to Seattle’s Craftsman bungalows, mid-century ranches, and older multi-family conversions. Lead paint assessment is standard practice on pre-1978 homes. ARIID Build coordinates licensed assessors as part of pre-construction on every applicable project, with results incorporated into the construction budget before demo begins.

Seattle’s neighborhoods each carry their own renovation character. Capitol Hill and Ballard projects trend toward urban density retrofits and ADU maximization. Queen Anne and Magnolia involve vertical homes on tight lots that require structural creativity. Laurelhurst, Madison Park, and Montlake involve larger-lot estates where the renovation scope competes with teardown economics — and often wins.

Frequently Asked Questions About Seattle Home Remodeling

Q: How long do home remodeling permits take in Seattle, WA?
A: Simple residential alterations may qualify for over-the-counter review in 4–10 weeks. Projects with structural changes, additions, ADUs, or homes in designated historic districts require full plan review — commonly 10–20 weeks or longer during peak SDCI volume. ARIID Build submits at the earliest possible design phase to prevent timeline compression.

Q: Do older Seattle homes require special assessments before remodeling?
A: Yes. Washington State requires asbestos survey and abatement for renovation work on materials installed before 1980 — applicable to many Seattle Craftsman bungalows and mid-century homes. Lead paint assessment is also recommended for pre-1978 homes. ARIID Build coordinates licensed assessments as part of pre-construction on applicable projects.

Q: Can you add an ADU to my Seattle property?
A: In many cases, yes. Seattle has relatively permissive ADU rules, including attached ADUs, detached ADUs, and backyard cottages. Lot size, existing structures, and zoning determine what’s feasible — we evaluate this during initial consultation.

Q: How long does a whole-home remodel in Seattle take?
A: Scope determines timeline. A focused multi-room remodel might run 4 to 6 months. A comprehensive renovation involving structural changes, new systems, and full permitting can take 8 to 14 months.

Q: How much does home remodeling in Seattle cost?
A: Multi-room updates typically start around $180,000. Full home renovations on larger Seattle properties run $400,000 to $900,000 depending on scope, existing conditions, and finish level.

Q: What makes ARIID different from other Seattle remodeling contractors?
A: We operate as a true design-build firm — design and construction under one team, with Ariana Adireh Anderson’s 25 years of experience and two National NKBA awards guiding every project.

Seattle homes range from 1930s Tudors to 2020 townhouses, and remodeling them well requires familiarity with how each era was actually built. We’ve worked across the city’s neighborhoods long enough to anticipate what’s behind the walls.

Remodeling a Seattle Home Is Its Own Discipline

Seattle’s residential architecture tells a complicated story. Walk through Laurelhurst and you’ll see 1930s Tudor revivals beside 1960s split-levels beside recent tear-down rebuilds. Head to Beacon Hill and the housing stock shifts again — modest postwar cottages, newer multifamily construction, and everything in between. Whole-home remodeling in this city requires genuine familiarity with how Seattle houses were built, not just how they look from the street.

We’ve spent decades working across Seattle’s varied neighborhoods, which means we recognize the signs — original fir floors hiding under carpet, older electrical panels that need upgrading before any significant kitchen or bathroom work begins, lot setback conditions that affect addition possibilities. This institutional knowledge doesn’t show up in a bid, but it shows up throughout a project.

Why Seattle Homeowners Remodel Rather Than Move

Seattle’s real estate market has made the math on moving increasingly difficult. Buying into a better house in Magnolia or Madison Park often means a significant price jump with higher interest rates layered on top. Many homeowners find it makes more financial and emotional sense to transform the home they’re already in — especially when that home has good bones, a lot size that allows for expansion, or a location that would be expensive to replicate.

We also see a recurring pattern: homeowners who purchased in the 2000s or 2010s, have equity, and want to finally address deferred updates — the outdated kitchen, the single bathroom serving a growing family, the garage that could become a functional ADU. These aren’t cosmetic projects. They’re substantive reinvestments in how a family lives.

What Whole-Home Remodeling Involves in Seattle

City of Seattle permitting is thorough and non-negotiable. Structural changes, electrical panel upgrades, plumbing reroutes, additions — all require permits and inspections. We manage the permitting process from first application through final sign-off. Seattle’s SDCI reviews plans carefully, especially for projects involving lot coverage, ADUs, or historic properties. Whole-home remodels in Seattle typically range from $250,000 for a focused multi-room update in a 1,500-square-foot home up to $800,000 or more for a comprehensive renovation of a larger Eastlake or Madrona property. Scope drives cost, and we define scope clearly at the outset.

Seattle Neighborhoods We Serve

Some of Seattle’s most architecturally significant homes sit on Queen Anne Hill. Victorian-era detailing, original millwork, period-appropriate character that clients want to preserve while updating kitchens, bathrooms, and living systems. We approach these homes with respect for what’s already there — not as blank canvases for contemporary intervention, but as structures with histories worth honoring.

Laurelhurst and Sand Point are high-value, family-oriented neighborhoods with a mix of mid-century homes and newer construction on larger lots. Whole-home remodels here often include kitchen expansions, primary suite additions, and ADU conversions — projects that require coordination between our design team and city planning. Capitol Hill, First Hill, and Central District bring urban density, smaller lots, older buildings, and a homeowner demographic that skews younger and design-forward. Projects here tend to emphasize open-plan conversions, ADU development, and comprehensive updates of older properties.

Kirkland Home Remodeling Is About How You Live in This City, Not How You’ll Eventually Sell It

Kirkland has one of the most livable neighborhood structures of any city on the Eastside — walkable downtown, multiple distinct residential areas each with their own character, a genuine waterfront, and a tech-sector population that works from home more than almost anywhere in the region. That last point matters for home remodeling. When you spend 40–60 hours a week inside your home, the layout, the light, the flow between kitchen and living space, and the quality of the primary suite stop being abstract preferences and become daily quality-of-life decisions. Kirkland homeowners who remodel are not staging for a future buyer. They are fixing what does not work for the way they actually live right now.

The City of Kirkland Building Division is one of the more efficient permit offices on the Eastside. It offers over-the-counter review for standard projects and has moved most residential submittals to an eReview system. Standard kitchen and bath remodel permits typically run 3–5 weeks in review. ADU projects and larger structural scopes — including additions and load-bearing wall removals — run 5–8 weeks. Kirkland’s ADU ordinance is also relatively permissive compared to neighboring cities, making accessory dwelling units a more frequently viable scope on Kirkland properties than elsewhere on the Eastside.

The housing stock in Kirkland is genuinely varied by sub-area. Juanita and Houghton waterfront properties are estate-scale projects with lake views as the primary design brief. Norkirk and Market Kirkland have 1950s–70s ramblers and traditional homes with original kitchens, closed floor plans, and electrical systems that require assessment before finalizing renovation scope. Rose Hill and Lakeview have a mix of 1980s–90s construction where the work is primarily finish-forward. ARIID Build works across all of these sub-markets and scopes each project for the specific property and neighborhood — not with a generic proposal.

Home Remodeling in Mercer Island, WA

Mercer Island stands apart, surrounded by Lake Washington and home to some of the region’s most remarkable residences. Homeowners here understand quality and recognize when a space no longer lives up to its setting or potential. ARIID Build & Remodel helps bridge that gap with integrity and expertise. Our design-build team brings design sophistication, construction precision, and complete accountability to every Mercer Island renovation, ensuring results that honor both the property and the investment it represents.

Home Remodeling Mercer Island

Working on homes in Mercer Island is something we take seriously—not because it sounds impressive, but because these properties genuinely deserve to be treated that way. The architectural range here is remarkable: mid-century classics along West Mercer Way that carry decades of accumulated character; contemporary estates on the Island’s interior that demand a precision of finish and detail most contractors aren’t equipped to deliver; newer construction homes where builder-grade choices have always sat slightly at odds with what the location deserves. At ARIID Build & Remodel, our home remodeling services are designed to serve all of those contexts with equal intelligence and craft. We keep design and construction under one roof, which means the vision developed in the design phase doesn’t get diluted by the time it reaches the job site—it gets realized, precisely and without apology.

Why Remodel Your Mercer Island Home?

Mercer Island homeowners don’t usually come to us because their home is failing them in obvious ways. They come to us because they have a clear sense of what their home could be—and an equally clear sense that it isn’t there yet. The gap between those two things is where we do our best work. The motivations we hear most consistently from clients on the Island:

The home has views, setting, and architectural bones that deserve an interior to match—and the interior hasn’t caught up yet. That disconnect bothers them every day, and they’re finally ready to resolve it properly.
A change in how they live—children who have left, a partner who works from home, a lifestyle that has evolved to prioritize entertaining or privacy or both—has revealed limitations in the existing floor plan that thoughtful design can permanently fix.
They’ve acquired a Mercer Island property with enormous potential and finishes that were never worthy of the location, and they want to bring it fully in line with its true caliber before making it truly theirs.
They’ve been investing in this home for years, doing one room at a time, and they’re ready to take a whole-home view and get it right in a way that actually coheres from room to room.

If you’re still in the early stages of defining what your renovation should look like, our guide on what homeowners need to consider before starting a remodel is a genuinely useful starting point before we sit down together for the first time.

ARIID Build & Remodel: Mercer Island Home Remodeling Experts

Mercer Island homes require a contractor who operates at a different level—one with the design range to work sensitively and intelligently across a wide variety of architectural styles, the construction discipline to execute at the standard these properties demand, and the structural integrity to take full ownership of the outcome from the first concept through the last detail. As a dedicated design-build firm, ARIID is built for exactly this kind of work. Our design-build team keeps design and construction fully integrated—the designers who conceive your renovation are involved in its execution, which means nothing important gets lost between the drawing and the build, and nothing gets compromised to make the construction easier. For homes of this caliber, that continuity isn’t a nice-to-have. It’s the baseline requirement. See what that standard produces across a range of our completed projects in our completed project gallery.

Full House Remodeling – Comprehensive whole-home transformations that address every room, system, material, and detail with the same unwavering level of design intelligence and construction quality throughout.
Kitchen Remodeling – Kitchens designed with genuine architectural consideration—custom cabinetry, natural stone surfaces, integrated appliances, and layouts that honor the home’s character while delivering fully modern performance.
Bathroom Remodeling – Master bath retreats that bring hotel-level luxury and genuine calm to the most private space in your home, designed and built to a standard that holds up for decades.
Home Additions – Architecturally considered expansions that add meaningful living space while integrating so seamlessly with the existing structure that the addition looks like it was always there.
Living & Dining Room Renovations – Open, light-filled spaces that connect to Mercer Island’s remarkable natural setting, flow intuitively through the home, and serve the full range of daily and social life.
Primary Suite Renovations – Truly private retreats—spa bathrooms, generous dressing rooms, considered lighting—designed to make the beginning and end of every day feel genuinely restorative rather than merely adequate.
Basement & Bonus Room Conversions – Purposeful transformations of underutilized space into rooms that earn their place in a home of this quality—home theaters, wine cellars, guest suites, or whatever purpose best serves your household.
Interior Design & Finish Selection – Expert material, finish, and fixture guidance that creates a coherent, considered design language across the entire home rather than a collection of room-by-room decisions that never quite add up to a whole.

Whether your project is focused on a single spectacular transformation or encompasses a comprehensive reimagining of the entire home, our full-service home remodeling approach ensures every element is thoughtfully integrated and executed to the same uncompromising standard.

Neighborhoods We Serve on Mercer Island

Mercer Island is compact but genuinely varied—in its architecture, its lot character, and the specific renovation challenges each neighborhood presents. We’re experienced working throughout the Island, including:

West Mercer Way Corridor – Iconic lakefront and hillside properties where renovation decisions need to be made with the views, the light, and the home’s architectural legacy all held in mind simultaneously.
East Mercer Way – Established estates and mid-century homes where thoughtful renovation honors decades of accumulated character while bringing the home’s performance and finishes fully into the present.
Island Crest – Family-oriented interiors where renovation balances genuine elegance with the practical, lived-in warmth that a home built for real family life actually requires.
North End – Newer construction homes where builder-grade choices have never quite matched the property’s potential, and where a focused renovation delivers the personalization and quality the location deserves.
South End – Wooded, private properties where renovation design draws on the natural setting—organic materials, considered proportions, and a deep connection to the landscape that feels earned.
Downtown Mercer Island – Condos and townhomes where every design decision is a space-planning decision—intelligent, precise, and executed to a luxury standard within a more compact footprint.
Current Home Remodeling Trends on Mercer Island

Mercer Island homeowners don’t need to be told what’s trending. They generally already know—and they’re appropriately skeptical of anything that looks like it will date in five years. What we see most in Island renovations right now is a clear preference for the timeless over the trendy: spaces that are architecturally considered, materially rich, and built with enough care that they improve rather than diminish over time. The specific directions we’re working in most frequently right now:

View-First Design that treats the landscape beyond the windows as the most important element of every room—orienting layouts, positioning openings, and selecting materials to frame and honor what Lake Washington and the Cascades offer from every property on this Island.
Whole-Home Architectural Cohesion where the renovation is used as an opportunity to develop a single, considered material and finish language that carries consistently from the entry through every room—so the home finally feels intentional in the way its setting always has.
Primary Suite Expansions and Transformations that treat the master bedroom as the deeply private, genuinely luxurious space a Mercer Island home should offer—not a nice bedroom, but a real retreat.
Indoor-Outdoor Living Integration through folding or sliding glass systems, covered terrace expansions, and seamless material transitions that extend the home into its remarkable outdoor setting during the months that allow it.
Bespoke Kitchen Renovations that treat the kitchen as an architectural element rather than a functional box—custom cabinetry with genuine proportional thought, natural stone with real visual character, and appliance integration that disappears into the design.
Smart Home Infrastructure woven into the renovation from the start—lighting, climate, security, and audio-visual systems that work together as a single, intuitive ecosystem rather than a collection of incompatible afterthoughts.

For more context on where luxury home renovation is heading regionally, our journal on the most important features of a luxury home remodel is worth reading—as is our 2026 home remodeling tips from our team.

Home Remodeling Costs on Mercer Island

Mercer Island homeowners approach cost conversations with the same clarity and directness they bring to everything else. We appreciate that—and we operate the same way. A renovation at this level is a significant investment, and it should be treated as one: with full transparency about what it costs, why it costs what it costs, and where the investment will have the greatest impact on the finished home. We never provide vague estimates designed to secure the project and expand once work begins. We provide clear, itemized breakdowns from the very first conversation, we explain every line, and we’re honest about the difference between where you can invest thoughtfully and where premium spending creates the most meaningful return. A focused single-room renovation and a comprehensive whole-home transformation are genuinely different projects at genuinely different investment levels—and we’ll always be clear about that before you make any decisions. Our post on why hiring a professional remodeling contractor matters explains what separates a contractor worth trusting from one worth avoiding—regardless of where the price falls.

Why Choose ARIID Build & Remodel?

There is no more exacting test of what a design-build firm is actually capable of than working on a home in Mercer Island. The properties are architecturally significant. The investments are substantial. The expectations are, appropriately, absolute. Our design-build team doesn’t find that daunting. We find it clarifying—because it removes any ambiguity about the standard the work needs to meet. We don’t approach Mercer Island projects as opportunities to be managed. We approach them as homes to be genuinely honored—and we bring everything that requires, from the design intelligence to the construction precision to the professional discretion that homeowners on this Island quite reasonably expect. What our Mercer Island clients consistently tell us they value most:

Design That Starts With the Home — we don’t impose a preferred aesthetic or pull from a template library. Every decision begins with a deep understanding of the home’s architecture, its setting, and the standard its history and location set for everything that happens inside it.
Craftsmanship That Matches the Investment — the quality of every material, the precision of every installation, and the care taken with every detail reflects the level of the home it’s going into—not a generic standard applied regardless of context.
Complete Project Ownership — one integrated team holds full responsibility for the outcome from the first concept sketch to the final walkthrough. No gaps, no handoffs, no moments where accountability becomes unclear.
Discretion and Professionalism — Mercer Island homeowners value privacy, minimal disruption to their household, and a contractor team that treats the property with the same respect its owners do. That’s not a policy we have to enforce. It’s simply how we operate.

We’ve written honestly about how to choose the best home remodeling contractor for a project of this significance—and we stand behind every criterion we put in it as the standard ARIID holds itself to.

Start Your Mercer Island Home Remodel Today

A home on Mercer Island is one of the most significant investments a person can make—in financial terms, yes, but more fundamentally in terms of how you intend to live. The renovation it deserves should honor that completely. With ARIID Build & Remodel, you have a design-build partner who understands what’s at stake, has the skill and discipline to deliver at that level, and takes as much pride in the finished result as you will.

Schedule your private consultation today and let’s begin designing a Mercer Island home that is truly worthy of everything the Island—and your investment in it—represents.

Island Logistics Add Cost and Complexity to Every Mercer Island Home Remodel — Unless Your Contractor Plans Around Them

Mercer Island is connected to the mainland by two I-90 bridges and nothing else. That geography is part of the island’s appeal — the separation creates a neighborhood character that is genuinely distinct from the surrounding Eastside cities. It also creates a set of logistical realities that every contractor working on the island has to navigate. Material deliveries cross the bridge. Subcontractors cross the bridge. County inspectors cross the bridge. Peak I-90 traffic directly affects delivery windows, daily schedule compression, and the ability to get inspection approvals on a predictable timeline. Contractors who do not account for these factors at the proposal stage surface them as surprises mid-construction. ARIID Build builds island logistics into every Mercer Island project budget and schedule from day one.

The City of Mercer Island Development Services office is relatively compact, consistent with the island’s residential character. All permitted residential work must be performed by licensed contractors — owner-builder permits are not available for the scope typical in a full home remodel. Standard remodel permits run 3–5 weeks in review. Structural additions and ADU projects run 6–10 weeks. ARIID Build is fully licensed and manages the complete submittal process, including inspection coordination with inspectors who also have to cross the bridge.

Mercer Island’s housing stock is primarily 1950s–80s, with a concentration of mid-century homes on large wooded lots on the North End and a mix of newer construction mixed into the South End. North End homes in particular are candidates for serious reconfiguration — closed floor plans, undersized primary suites, and kitchens that were designed in a different era of how families eat and entertain. The lake views that many of these homes have are underutilized by the original layout. ARIID Build redesigns around the view as the primary brief, using open-plan conversion and strategic window and door placement to make the view the organizing principle of the renovated space.

Why does home remodeling on Mercer Island cost more than comparable Eastside projects?
All contractors, materials, and inspectors cross the I-90 bridge — adding logistics time and cost to every project phase. ARIID Build builds these factors into project budgets and schedules upfront rather than surfacing them as surprises.

What are the permit rules for home remodeling on Mercer Island?
City of Mercer Island Development Services requires all permitted residential work to use licensed contractors — owner-builder permits are not available. Review runs 3–5 weeks for standard scope; structural additions and ADUs run 6–10 weeks.

What does home remodeling cost on Mercer Island, WA?
Single-room projects run 110,000 to 220,000 dollars; multi-room projects run 300,000 to 650,000 dollars; whole-home remodels on North End estates range from 600,000 to 2,000,000 dollars or more.
