Our People
Kiel Kellow

OWNER

Kiel Kellow is an anomaly in the building trade, a design focused builder who believes that estimating and design should always go hand in hand. As the leader of Kellow Construction, Kiel’s approach ensures that all design work is not just creative and beautiful, but practical and aligned with the client’s investment range. This philosophy reduces the typical back and forth between design and construction, making the process more efficient and cohesive.

A highly attuned business owner, Kiel is a naturally calm and effective leader who values ethics, hard work, and communication above all else. He is not your typical builder, he genuinely loves the process of guiding clients through projects that might initially feel overwhelming or out of reach. Helping people accomplish something transformative while balancing design vision with real world practicality is one of his greatest skills.

Kiel grew up in both Tillamook County, Oregon, and Bainbridge Island, Washington. He honed his carpentry skills while living on his 1934 wooden sailboat in the Bainbridge harbor, working on boats, high end custom homes, and in a cabinet shop crafting all things wood. Eventually, he recognized that his passion for client collaboration and project implementation meant starting his own business.

After moving to Portland, Oregon, Kiel became a lead carpenter with an award winning design/build firm specializing in restaurant build outs. There, he mastered the art of integrating complex architectural details into functional spaces, particularly in light commercial projects.

Today, as the owner of Kellow Construction, Kiel brings together design, estimating, and building with a commitment to quality craftsmanship and client satisfaction. His philosophy is simple: build classic structures that endure and create spaces people love. At the heart of it all, Kiel uses his skills to help people bring their dreams to life, combining creativity with practical execution to make the process as rewarding as the final result.

Emily Kellow

OFFICE MANAGER Emily Kellow was born and raised in Santa Barbara and cares deeply about this community. She attended Starr King Parent Child Workshop, Monte Vista Grammar School, La Colina Junior High, and San Marcos High School. Like many locals, she spent her summers on the beach as a Junior Lifeguard, and she still feels grateful every day to live and raise her family in a place with such extraordinary natural beauty and public lands. After graduating from UC Davis in 2007, Emily moved to Portland, Oregon for what she thought would be a short adventure. Instead, she ended up spending more than a decade there building and running her own residential real estate brokerage. Helping people buy, sell, lease, and renovate the amazing older homes of Portland. That experience gave her a deep appreciation for the complexity of construction projects and the importance of clear communication, strong systems, and financial stewardship. Today at Kellow Construction, Emily works mostly behind the scenes making sure the company runs smoothly for clients and the team alike. She oversees accounting, contracts, insurance, payroll, purchasing, and the systems that keep projects organized and moving forward. If something requires patience, persistence, or a very long hold time on the phone, Emily is usually the one handling it. Emily enjoys helping bring a sense of order and calm to complex projects so clients can focus on the exciting parts of building or remodeling their homes. Outside of work, she loves long walks without a destination, beach days with friends and children, podcasts and audiobooks, cultivating peace and positivity, and volunteering at her son’s neighborhood public school.

Jason

PROJECT MANAGER

Born and raised on the Upper East Side of Santa Barbara, and a proud Santa Barbara Don, Jason brings over 15 years of hands-on carpentry experience to his role as PM. He manages scopes, the day to day activity on site, oversees our subcontractors and production team, and often jumps in with tools on to lend a hand wherever needed.

When he's not on the job, Jason enjoys spending time with his wife Ashley, going on long bike rides, and enjoying the company of his many animals, all while living in the town he’s proud to call home.

Rudy

Superintendent

Rudy grew up in Santa Barbara and has been part of the local construction scene since the days when Paseo Nuevo Mall was still Piccadilly Square, he even worked on the project himself. With more than two decades of experience supervising and managing residential remodels, Rudy brings a deep understanding of what it takes to keep projects organized, efficient, and running smoothly. His sharp eye for quality craftsmanship and well run job sites makes him a natural fit for the Kellow Construction team and helps ensure our projects stay on schedule and on budget. At Kellow Construction, Rudy plays a key role in supporting the kind of thoughtful, high quality work our clients expect. Outside of work, he enjoys spending time with his wife, a high school teacher at Dos Pueblos High School, and their daughter. He also plays drums and music at church on Sundays and enjoys making the most of the beautiful hometown he’s proud to call home, Santa Barbara.

Tara
Designer

A San Diego native, she earned her BFA in Interior Architecture from Chico State before making her way to Santa Barbara, a place she now feels incredibly lucky to call home. A natural people person, she believes that great design starts with genuine relationships and enjoys getting to know her clients and the people she works alongside.

At Kellow Construction, she brings a thoughtful and personal approach to design, creating spaces that feel unique to each client while making the experience along the way just as meaningful as the finished result.

Outside of work, she loves spending time with friends, trying new restaurants and foods, traveling, camping in Big Sur, and enjoying everything life along the California coast has to offer.

Our Carpenters

Kellow Construction runs a team of highly skilled carpenters and foremen in the field. Our strict and comprehensive hiring process has proven to be an effective tool at attracting the best people, and repelling those that are not a great fit. We are uncompromising in our hiring process, and make sure that all our team members commit to adhering strictly to our company values with no exceptions. You can be certain that anyone who works for us has “it” and will handle your project with the care, attention, and respect it deserves.

Logan
Fabian
OFFICE STAFF
Sasha

OFFICE ASSISTANT

Sasha hails from our close neighbor, Santa Maria! She is currently a devoted student at UCSB, pursuing a degree in Accounting and Finance. Between studying and working she doesn’t have time for much else, but when she can she loves to surf, drink coffee and enjoy all that Santa Barbara has to offer. She is also a world famous jewelry maker and makes beautiful threaded pieces you can check them out here. When Sasha is working you can always find the office cat Frannie sitting on her lap. She assists Emily in pretty much everything she does and is an absolute WHIP when it comes to the numbers, and also making things look beautiful. She is a critical component that keeps Kellow Construction running smooth as silk.

Subcontractors

We partner with local subcontractors and vendors who have a commitment to excellence just like us. Our subs spend time upfront studying the site conditions and the scope of work. They do things right the first time, minimizing project management and oversight fees from us. We bring in the A-Teams which means you are in good hands, all the way down the line.

Conscientious
Construction

Kellow Construction is currently the only contractor in California to hold the Earth Advantage Sustainable Homes Professionals (SHP) designation. We are proud to hold this title and hope it displays our commitment to building and running our company in a way that will reduce not only our carbon footprint, but also our client’s. Read more about the Earth Advantage SHP program or download a copy of our certificate.

KELLOW CONSTRUCTION · DESIGN-BUILD · SANTA BARBARA, CA
Santa Barbara Home Remodeling and Renovation

Kellow Construction is a licensed general contractor in Santa Barbara, specializing in home renovation and the design-build process. As a design build firm, we’re a full service team for the entire project. We have architectural design, interior design Santa Barbara homeowners trust, planning, permitting, and construction. Our model has proven time and again that there is real power, efficiency, and a overall better client experience in having the designers and the builders all on the same team.

High-Touch, Small-Team Experience on Large Projects: Big enough and experienced to handle complex, high-end projects.

Small enough that homeowners still get senior attention.

Most of our clients come to us with a vision for their home remodeling project and the desire to have a different and better experience than the traditional design bid build model that they may have been frustrated with in the past. We develop your design, value engineer it throughout the process, and present a fixed price before construction begins, so you know exactly what you're getting, and exactly what it costs, before we ever break ground. Price certainty, a strong process, and a highly experienced team is what sets us apart.

START THE CONVERSATION
HOW IT WORKS
A thoughtful process, start to finish

A clear, guided path from concept to completion. Design, budget, permitting, and construction are considered together from the beginning, so you always know where you are, what comes next, and how each decision affects the whole project.

Initial Consultation

We start with a conversation about your home, your goals, your vision, and your investment range. We’ll talk through what you’re hoping to accomplish, how our design-build process works, and whether your project feels like the right fit for both of us.

No pressure. Just an honest first conversation and a clear next step.

Design Phase 1

Before diving into design, we take a closer look at the realities of your project—your existing home, priorities, constraints, permitting considerations, and investment range.

We explore what’s possible and begin aligning scope, design ambitions, and budget early, when there is still plenty of room to make thoughtful decisions.

The goal is a shared vision and a realistic path forward before significant design work begins.

Design Phase 2

With a Design Agreement in place, our in-house design team turns that direction into a real project—developing plans, layouts, materials, fixtures, finishes, and the details that make the home yours.

Because the people designing your project are working alongside the people who will ultimately build it, constructability and cost are part of the conversation throughout design—not something we discover at the end.

What we design should be beautiful, buildable, and aligned with the investment you’ve established.

Documents and Permitting

As the design comes together, we develop the technical drawings and specifications needed to build it, coordinate consultants and engineering, and guide the project through permitting.

At the same time, selections and details continue to be documented so the project becomes increasingly defined and trackable.

By the time we move into final pricing, we know what we’re building—not just what we hope to build.

Fixed-Price Contract

Once the scope is fully defined, selections are dialed in, and the project is ready to build, we present a fixed-price construction contract.

We don’t ask you to commit to construction based on a rough estimate and figure out the details later. The work of design, documentation, selections, and pricing happens first.

You’ll know exactly what you’re building—and exactly what it costs—before we break ground.

Construction

When construction begins, the project doesn’t get handed off to a completely different team. Your project manager and site superintendent work from the plans, selections, budget, and decisions developed throughout the design process.

They oversee the schedule, trades, craftsmanship, jobsite, and communication, with regular updates and clear accountability along the way.

One integrated team, carrying the project from the first conversation through the final details of your home.

Our Warranty

Our comprehensive warranty gives you peace of mind that we will be there for you long after your project is completed.

START THE CONVERSATION
WHY DESIGN BUILD?
What the design-build model provides

The advantages of a design-build versus GC and architect are:

From start to finish, you have experienced and trusted advisors advocating for you and your home, and educated in the right ways to make the dream a reality.

We have the unique ability to marry the client’s desires and needs with the budget throughout the entire process. Pricing and financial management are part of what we do with you, that can is front and center, and not kicked down the road after too many design dollars have been spent.

There’s streamlined and consistent communication between designers and the trades who will actually be on your project. We’ve curated relationships with reliable, quality craftspeople, who have been vetted to meet our high standards.

Price Certainty

We work on a fixed price single number construction contract. All selections and every last detail is taken into account when pricing your project so you can go into your build with the confidence that fixed price brings.

A Proven, Predictable Process

Design build is a unique skill set. We geek out on order, communication, and a clear sequence and we're contractors, so we balance that architectural rigor with real-world practicality and a no nonsense approach. Every phase follows a defined path, our designers are tempered with real life constraints and deadlines of a production and estimating team, and we keep you informed at every step.

Budget Alignment Throughout Design

We manage your goals, needs, and budget against the design from day one, value engineering your project throughout the process to keep selections aligned with investment and project goals, and in accordance with the overall vision, without compromising what you came to us for. Our goal is that your investment in design is razor sharp with nothing presented to you that would not be possible in your unique real world application.

One Team, Full Accountability

Your designer works full time directly with your project manager and field team. There's no gap between who designed it and who's building it, and your designer is steeped in our process and our construction driven world.. When a question comes up, one team answers it together, with a hive mind that you just can’t get in a more fractured design bid (hope) build model. We are dreamers grounded in reality, which helps your design and construction dollars go further.

Local Expertise

We've navigated Santa Barbara's unique permitting processes and requirements, Montecito remodeling and overlay regulations, and Hope Ranch project considerations across dozens of projects. That familiarity informs how we approach feasibility and timeline from the very first conversation. Our entire team lives, works and breathes Santa Barbara remodeling, construction and design which is a client advantage and resource.

Clarity Before Commitment

We operate on fixed price contract. We don't ask you to commit to construction until the scope is fully defined, priced and selections are dialed and trackable. You'll know exactly what you're building, and exactly what it costs, before we break ground.

WHAT WE BUILD
Design-build services
Whole House Remodels

Full-scope Santa Barbara home remodeling transformations, from gut renovation to thoughtful updates that make your whole home work the way your life does.

Kitchen Design and Remodel

We design and build kitchens worth cooking in — Santa Barbara kitchen remodeling from concept through construction, with layouts that work, finishes that hold up, and details that feel like they were always there.

Bath Design and Remodel

Santa Barbara bathroom remodeling done right — spa-quality bathrooms designed and built by the same team. We handle layout, plumbing, tile, and every detail that makes the difference between fine and exceptional.

Home Additions

We design and build additions that feel like they've always been part of your home — from the first sketch through permits, construction, and close-out.

LET'S TALK

Kellow Construction provides high end home remodeling services in Santa Barbara and Montecito for homeowners planning comprehensive, design led renovations. As a trusted Santa Barbara home remodeling contractor, we specialize in projects that go beyond single room updates, reimagining how the entire home functions, flows, and feels.

Our home remodel service is ideal for clients undertaking a full home renovation, major layout changes, or multi space remodels that require thoughtful planning, architectural coordination, and disciplined execution.

What Defines a Kellow Construction Home Remodel
View fullsize

Unlike kitchen or bathroom remodels, a home remodel addresses the house as a complete system. These projects often involve multiple spaces, structural changes, and long-term planning, making experience, process, and design leadership essential.

Our home remodeling service commonly includes: 

Whole house renovations and phased remodels

Structural modifications and reconfiguration

Coordinated updates across kitchens, bathrooms, living areas, and bedrooms

Architectural restoration and modernization

Systems upgrades integrated into a cohesive plan

As a design build home remodeling contractor, we ensure that every decision supports both the overall vision and the practical realities of construction.

A Design-Build Process Built for Complex Remodels

Home remodeling requires more than construction expertise, it requires foresight, coordination, and design clarity from the very beginning.

Our design-build model brings design, planning, and construction under one roof, allowing us to:

Evaluate feasibility early

Align design intent with execution

Reduce uncertainty during construction

Maintain continuity from concept through completion

Clients benefit from a guided, transparent experience where decisions are made intentionally and the process feels structured, not reactive.

Preserve and elevate architectural details

As an experienced home remodeler in Santa Barbara, our role is to guide these decisions with clarity, care, and craftsmanship.

Kitchen Remodeling

Specialist ensure that each one of your kitchen remodeling jobs are completed beyond expectations

CONTACT US
KITCHEN REMODELING DONE RIGHT
Best Kitchen Remodeling in Palm Beach County

At North2South Renovations, we believe the kitchen is more than just a place to cook — it’s the heart of your home. It’s where families gather, stories are shared, and memories are made. That’s why our team specializes in kitchen remodeling services across Palm Beach County, delivering beautifully designed spaces that blend function, comfort, and modern style. Whether you’re looking to upgrade outdated finishes, expand your layout, or create a fully custom dream kitchen, we bring precision, creativity, and craftsmanship to every project.

Custom Kitchen Design & Planning

Every great kitchen starts with a plan.

Custom Island Installs

We want to ensure each project has the perfect feel and look

Appliance Installs

Everyone home is different and we understand that

WHAT IS INCLUDED

Kitchen Backsplash Installation
Kitchen Flooring Options

Materials
Choose from a wide selection of premium materials, including full custom shaker cabinets or semi-custom white options.
You can also select from our range of in-house countertops, such as quartz, quartzite, and granite.
Consultation
Ensuring that you get the correct pricing and equipment.
You can also select from our range of in-house countertops, such as quartz, quartzite, and granite.
Fabrication
Our team manufactures your cabinets and fabricates your countertops in-house to ensure the highest quality and precision.
We want to ensure that your project is custom, in all aspects
Installation
Once everything is ready, our experts handle the installation of your cabinets, countertops, and any necessary structural modifications.
We begin with a consultation to understand your needs, preferences, and vision for your kitchen. Our design team will help create a custom plan that meets both your functional and aesthetic goals.

A kitchen remodel is one of the most rewarding investments a homeowner can make — not only for its ability to elevate the look and feel of your home, but also for the value it adds. At North2South Renovations, we specialize in turning outdated kitchens into modern, functional spaces that reflect your personal style and daily needs. Whether it’s reconfiguring the layout for better flow, upgrading cabinets and countertops, or integrating the latest appliances, our team approaches every project with precision, creativity, and a focus on long-term quality. We believe your kitchen should be more than beautiful — it should make cooking, entertaining, and everyday living easier and more enjoyable.

Every kitchen remodel we take on begins with a thoughtful design process. Our experienced designers work closely with you to understand your goals, preferences, and budget before bringing your ideas to life through 3D renderings and material selections. From custom cabinetry and durable quartz countertops to elegant backsplashes and ambient lighting, every element is chosen to balance form and function. Whether you prefer a sleek, contemporary kitchen or a warm, coastal-inspired design, North2South Renovations tailors every detail to your lifestyle while ensuring each component is installed with expert craftsmanship and care.

As a Certified General Contractor serving Palm Beach County, we take pride in handling every aspect of your remodel from start to finish — including permitting, inspections, and code compliance. Our team maintains clear communication throughout the process to ensure transparency, efficiency, and peace of mind. The result is a stunning, high-performance kitchen that enhances both your home’s appeal and your daily life. With North2South Renovations, you’re not just getting a new kitchen — you’re getting a space built to inspire, gather, and create lasting memories for years to come.

Palm Beach Counties Finest
Bathroom Remodeling

At North2South Renovations, we turn outdated bathrooms into elegant, functional retreats that elevate your home’s comfort and style. Serving all of Palm Beach County, our licensed and certified team specializes in full bathroom renovations — from modern walk-in showers and custom vanities to tile design and lighting upgrades. Every project is built with precision, quality craftsmanship, and materials designed to last in Florida’s coastal climate.

CONTACT US
PALM BEACH'S FINEST BATHROOM REMODELING CONTRACTOR
Transform Your Bathroom Into a Space of Comfort, Function, and Style

At North2South Renovations, we specialize in creating bathroom spaces that combine luxury design with everyday functionality. Whether you’re dreaming of a modern spa retreat, a sleek guest bath, or a full master suite transformation, our team brings craftsmanship, precision, and local expertise to every detail.
Proudly serving Boca Raton, Delray Beach, Boynton Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, and the surrounding areas, we help homeowners reimagine their bathrooms with top-quality materials, efficient layouts, and stunning finishes built to last in Florida’s coastal climate.

Consultation & Design

We start with an in-depth consultation to understand your goals, style preferences, and budget. Our designers craft a layout and visual plan that optimizes space, lighting, and function while reflecting your personal taste.

Demolition & Preparation

Old fixtures, tile, and flooring are carefully removed to prepare your space for new installations. We handle all debris removal and ensure your home stays clean and protected throughout the project.

Plumbing & Electrical

We upgrade or relocate pipes, drains, and electrical wiring to meet current code and functionality standards. This includes GFCI outlets, new lighting circuits, and shower or vanity plumbing.

OUR FRAMEWORK

From Concept to Completion — The North2South Renovations Story

North2South Renovations is a full-service remodeling company dedicated to transforming homes across South Florida with precision, creativity, and craftsmanship. From kitchen and bathroom remodels to complete home renovations, our team combines modern design with practical functionality to create spaces that truly reflect each client’s lifestyle. We take pride in managing every detail — from concept and planning to construction and finishing touches — ensuring a seamless experience and exceptional results. With years of experience, trusted local partnerships, and a passion for quality workmanship, North2South Renovations continues to set the standard for reliable, beautiful, and lasting home transformations across the region.

Our story

At North2South Renovations, our story began with a simple mission — to redefine what homeowners can expect from a bathroom and home remodeling company. Founded by Colby Matheny, our team set out to bring honesty, craftsmanship, and creativity back into the heart of South Florida’s renovation industry. From the very beginning, we’ve believed that every home has its own story — and our job is to help you write the next chapter with precision and style.

What we do

What started as a small local operation quickly grew into a trusted name for bathroom remodeling, kitchen renovations, and full home transformations across Palm Beach and Broward counties. Our success comes from our attention to detail, clear communication, and commitment to turning every client’s vision into reality. Whether it’s a luxury bathroom renovation, a modern kitchen design, or a complete home makeover, we approach each project with the same dedication and care we’d give our own home.

General Contracting in Palm Beach Florida

South Florida has some of the strictest building codes in the country — and for good reason. Here’s what homeowners in Palm Beach County should know before starting a major renovation:

Projects
Licensed General Contractor in Palm Beach County

When your project goes beyond a single room — a whole-home renovation, a structural change, an addition, or any job that requires permits and multiple trades working in sequence — you need more than a remodeler. You need a licensed general contractor who can take full responsibility for the project from the first drawing to the final inspection.

North2South Renovations is a fully licensed and insured Florida general contractor- License #CBC1269429- based in Palm Beach County, with 15 years of hands-on renovation experience across Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, and the surrounding communities. We manage the entire project — permitting, scheduling, subcontractors, inspections, and quality control — so you have one accountable point of contact from start to finish.

Construction Permitting and code compliance.

We prepare and submit permit applications with the Palm Beach County Building Division or your city's building department, coordinate required documents, and schedule every inspection through final approval.

Multi-trade coordination

Larger renovations involve electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians, drywall crews, tile setters, and finish carpenters — all of whom need to show up in the right order. We schedule, supervise, and quality-check every trade so the project moves without gaps or rework.

A Stress-Free Renovation Process
General Contracting
Frequently Asked Questions
Do I need a general contractor for my renovation in Palm Beach County?

If your project involves permits, structural changes, or multiple trades (electrical, plumbing, HVAC), Florida law and practicality both point to hiring a licensed GC. For single-scope cosmetic remodels, a licensed specialty contractor may be sufficient. We're happy to tell you honestly which one your project needs during a free consultation.

Whole Home Renovations in Palm Beach

When your home no longer matches your lifestyle, needs, or vision, renovation one room at a time may not be enough

Projects
Complete Home Remodeling Designed Around the Way You Live

North2South Renovations provides whole home renovation and complete home remodeling services throughout Palm Beach County. We help homeowners transform outdated, inefficient, and disconnected properties into cohesive living spaces designed around comfort, functionality, quality, and long-term value.

From reconfiguring interior layouts and creating open-concept living spaces to remodeling kitchens, bathrooms, flooring, lighting, custom cabinetry, and interior finishes, our team manages the many moving parts involved in a comprehensive home renovation.

Whole Home Kitchen Remodeling

For many whole home renovations, the kitchen becomes the centerpiece of the project. The kitchen influences surrounding living spaces, flooring selections, lighting plans, storage solutions, and the overall design direction of the home. North2South Renovations provides comprehensive kitchen remodeling services as part of complete home renovation projects.

Open-Concept Whole Home Renovations

Creating an open-concept floor plan is one of the most significant changes homeowners can make during a complete renovation. Removing or modifying interior walls can create better sightlines, improve natural light, and allow kitchens, dining rooms, and living areas to function as connected spaces.

A Stress-Free Renovation Process

How long does a whole home renovation take?

Whole home renovation timelines vary significantly depending on the size and complexity of the project.

Comprehensive renovations may take several months, particularly when projects involve structural modifications, kitchens, multiple bathrooms, flooring, custom cabinetry, mechanical improvements, and extensive finish work.

Welcome to North2South Renovations

Looking to transform your home or business with premium flooring solutions in Palm Beach? North2South Renovations delivers expert residential flooring installation and commercial flooring services tailored to your needs. From consultation to cleanup, our team ensures a seamless experience with every project.

We specialize in a wide variety of flooring installation services, including hardwood flooring, laminate flooring, vinyl plank flooring, tile flooring, carpet installation, and more.

Looking for expert flooring services in Palm Beach? North2South Renovations offers professional residential and commercial flooring installation, specializing in hardwood flooring, laminate flooring, vinyl plank flooring, tile flooring, carpet installation, and luxury vinyl tile (LVT). From waterproof and pet-friendly flooring to eco-friendly and scratch-resistant options, we provide low-maintenance flooring solutions built to last. Our full-service approach includes free consultations, custom flooring installation, floor refinishing, floor removal and replacement, and repair services. Whether you’re upgrading one room or your entire space, trust our experienced team to deliver beautiful, durable floors with top-rated service across Palm Beach County.

Call Today

Quality Life for You and Your Family
Custom
Flooring

At North2South Renovations, we proudly serve homeowners and businesses across Palm Beach County—including West Palm Beach, Boca Raton, Delray Beach, Boynton Beach, Wellington, and surrounding areas—with expert flooring installation services tailored to every style and need. Our team specializes in a wide variety of flooring options, from timeless hardwood flooring and eco-conscious engineered wood flooring to durable laminate flooring, luxury vinyl plank (LVP), and luxury vinyl tile (LVT) for waterproof, pet-friendly spaces. We also offer elegant tile flooring including porcelain, ceramic, and natural stone—ideal for Florida’s humid climate—as well as plush, sound-absorbing carpet installation for cozy interiors. For those seeking sustainable solutions, we install environmentally friendly bamboo flooring and cork flooring, along with low-maintenance options like peel-and-stick vinyl for rental or commercial use. In high-performance spaces such as home gyms or garages, we offer practical rubber and polished concrete flooring. Beyond installation, our full-service offerings include floor repair, floor refinishing, floor removal and replacement, and custom flooring installation for both residential and commercial flooring projects. Whether you’re seeking scratch-resistant, eco-friendly, or low-maintenance flooring, we bring craftsmanship and care to every job—delivering beautiful, lasting results across Palm Beach County.

Luxury Vinyl Plank (LVP) & Luxury Vinyl Tile (LVT)

Get the realistic look of wood or stone with waterproof flooring that’s built to last. These scratch-resistant floors are perfect for pet-friendly flooring needs and low-maintenance flooring options.

Laminate Flooring

Cost-effective and stylish, laminate flooring offers durable performance and realistic textures. Great for homes that need eco-friendly flooring options with fast turnaround times.

Engineered Wood Flooring

Enjoy the beauty of real wood with added structural stability. Engineered wood flooring resists humidity—ideal for South Florida homes.

Porcelain & Tile Flooring

Sleek, strong, and elegant, our tile flooring options are perfect for kitchens, bathrooms, and outdoor spaces. Choose from custom designs, backsplashes, and more.

Solid Hardwood Flooring

Classic, timeless, and adds value to any home. Sandable and refinishable over time.

Bamboo Flooring

A sustainable and eco-friendly hardwood alternative with a modern, clean look.

Terrazzo Flooring

Stylish and low-maintenance with a unique, speckled design—perfect for high-end spaces.

Stone Flooring (Travertine, Marble, Slate)

Natural beauty with a luxurious finish, perfect for upscale homes and exterior transitions.

At North2South Renovations, we specialize in expert flooring installations that transform any space into a beautiful and functional environment. Whether you’re upgrading to engineered wood, luxury vinyl plank (LVP), tile, laminate, or even carpet, our team ensures a seamless and precise installation process. We begin with a thorough consultation to understand your needs and preferences, then carefully prepare your space for installation, including any necessary floor removal and demolition. Our skilled professionals take great care to ensure each floor is installed with the highest level of craftsmanship, ensuring durability, precision, and aesthetic appeal. With attention to detail and a commitment to customer satisfaction, we’re dedicated to providing a flooring solution that suits your style and stands the test of time.

From the bustling streets of Downtown West Palm Beach to the tranquil neighborhoods of Jupiter, we’re committed to delivering high-quality, durable flooring that enhances the beauty and functionality of your home or business.

Do I need a permit to remodel my home in Boynton Beach?

Yes — most kitchen remodels, bathroom renovations, and structural work in Boynton Beach require permits through the City of Boynton Beach Building Department. Unlike some surrounding areas that fall under Palm Beach County jurisdiction, the city runs its own permitting operation with digital plan submission and review. Only minor cosmetic work like painting, flooring, and cabinetry not tied to a kitchen or bath remodel is exempt. As your licensed general contractor (License #CBC1269429), North2South Renovations handles the full permit process — application, plan review, corrections, and every required inspection — so your project stays compliant from day one.

Third-Generation Carpenter. Your Remodeler.

I'm Brad Zemke. My grandfather was a carpenter, my dad was a carpenter, and I've spent 20+ years learning this trade the right way. After 5 years as a B-52 crew chief in the Air Force, I started Pacific Remodeling in Puyallup in 2018 and brought that same discipline to every project I take on.

How Every Project Works

01

I come to your home, take measurements, and talk through what you want and what you can spend. No pressure. No sales pitch.

02
Design & Proposal

You get a detailed, fixed-price proposal with every line item spelled out: materials, labor, timeline. I use EstimationPro AI to build estimates, so the numbers match reality.

03
Build Day to Finish

I handle demo, framing, plumbing, electrical, tile, cabinetry, and finish work. One crew, daily updates, and the same standard on every single project.

Before I call it done, I walk every inch with you. If something isn't right, I fix it. The standard: would I be proud to show this to my own family?

Kitchen Remodeling
OUR #1 SERVICE
Kitchen Remodeling in Puyallup, WA

Transform your kitchen into the heart of your home with custom renovations by Puyallup's most trusted remodeling contractor.

WHAT'S INCLUDED
Our Kitchen Remodeling Services
Custom Cabinetry

Solid wood, thermofoil, and modern slab-style options. Soft-close hinges, pull-out shelves, and custom organization solutions tailored to your space.

Countertop Installation

Granite, quartz, marble, butcher block — precision templated and fabricated for flawless seams and perfect fit.

Kitchen Islands & Peninsulas

Additional storage, prep space, and seating designed around your floor plan. Waterfall edges, integrated sinks, and power outlets.

Flooring

Luxury vinyl plank, tile, and hardwood installed with proper subfloor preparation for a level, lasting finish.

Plumbing & Fixtures

Farmhouse sinks, touchless faucets, pot fillers, dishwasher hookups, and complete plumbing rough-ins for layout changes.

Electrical & Lighting

Recessed cans, under-cabinet LED strips, pendant fixtures, and dedicated appliance circuits to code.

Backsplash Installation

Subway tile, mosaic, natural stone, and large-format porcelain options professionally installed.

Layout Reconfiguration

Opening walls, moving plumbing stacks, and creating open-concept living spaces that maximize your kitchen's potential.

Why Choose Pacific Remodeling for Your Kitchen Renovation?

Your kitchen is more than a place to cook. It’s where your family gathers in the morning, where guests end up standing around the island during every party, and where you spend more time than any other room in the house. I’ve remodeled hundreds of kitchens across Puyallup and Pierce County since starting Pacific Remodeling in 2018, and every single project starts the same way: by listening to what’s actually bothering you about your current space.

Maybe the layout forces you to walk 15 feet between the sink and the stove. Maybe the cabinets are falling apart after 30 years. Maybe you just want a kitchen that feels like it belongs in your home and not in 1987. Whatever the reason, I treat every kitchen like I’m building it for my own family. That’s the standard my grandfather set when he taught me this trade, and it’s the standard I hold my crews to on every job.

Our Approach

Every kitchen remodel starts with a free in-home consultation where I listen to your goals, take measurements, discuss material options, and understand your budget. You’ll receive a detailed, fixed-price proposal with a clear scope of work and timeline. No surprises, no hidden fees.

Our crews handle every aspect of the renovation: demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, drywall, tile, cabinetry installation, countertop fabrication, painting, and final finish work. One team, one point of contact, one company accountable for the result.

What Happens Week by Week: Your Kitchen Remodel Timeline

One of the first things people ask me is, “How long is my kitchen going to be torn apart?” Fair question. Here’s what a typical full kitchen remodel looks like, broken down by week, so you know exactly what to expect.

Week 1: Demolition and Discovery We remove existing cabinets, countertops, flooring, and backsplash. This is also when we open up walls if you’re changing the layout. I always prepare clients for this week because it looks worse before it gets better. Old kitchens sometimes hide surprises behind the walls, like outdated wiring, water damage, or galvanized plumbing that needs replacing. We document everything and discuss any changes before moving forward.

Week 2: Rough-In Work Electrical, plumbing, and framing changes happen now. If you’re adding an island sink, moving the dishwasher, or installing a pot filler, this is when the supply lines, drain lines, and vent stacks get routed. We also pull permits from the City of Puyallup and schedule inspections for this phase. Any structural changes, like removing a load-bearing wall and installing a beam, happen during this week as well.

Weeks 3-4: Closing Walls and Cabinets After inspections pass, we hang new drywall, tape, mud, and sand. Then cabinets go in. This is where the kitchen starts to take shape and you can finally see the layout come to life. Cabinet installation typically takes 2-3 days for a standard kitchen. We level everything precisely because even a 1/16-inch gap shows on a finished cabinet run.

Week 5: Countertops and Tile Once cabinets are set, we template for countertops. Fabrication takes about 5-7 business days. While we wait, the backsplash tile goes up, flooring gets installed, and we handle detail work like trim and under-cabinet lighting.

Weeks 6-7: Countertop Install, Fixtures, and Finishing Countertops are set, sinks and faucets are connected, appliances get installed, and we handle all the final details: hardware, outlet covers, touch-up paint, and trim. I do a walkthrough with you to make sure every detail meets your expectations before we call the project complete.

Weeks 8-10 (if needed): Larger projects with structural changes, custom elements, or layout reconfigurations may extend the timeline. I always build a buffer into our schedule because I’d rather underpromise and overdeliver than the other way around.

Popular Kitchen Styles in Puyallup and Pierce County Homes

I’ve worked on just about every type of home in this area. The housing stock in Puyallup, South Hill, and the surrounding communities is heavily concentrated in the 1970s through 1990s. That means a lot of builders’ grade oak cabinets, laminate countertops, vinyl flooring, and layouts that were designed around appliances that don’t exist anymore.

Here’s what I see most often and what homeowners are choosing to replace them with:

1970s-1980s Ramblers and Split-Levels These kitchens are usually closed off from the dining and living areas with a pass-through window or a narrow doorway. The number one request I get is opening up the wall between the kitchen and living room to create an open-concept layout. Most of these walls are load-bearing, which means we need to install a properly sized LVL or steel beam. It adds $4,000-$13,000 to the project, but it completely transforms how the home feels.

1980s-1990s Two-Stories These homes often have more kitchen square footage but poor layouts. The island was an afterthought, the pantry is too small, and the lighting is a single fluorescent box in the center of the ceiling. We typically reconfigure the island for better flow, add pull-out pantry storage, and replace that fluorescent fixture with a combination of recessed cans and pendant lights.

Newer Construction (2000s+) These kitchens have better bones but dated finishes. Cabinet refacing, new countertops, a modern backsplash, and updated hardware can give these kitchens a completely new look for $16,000-$40,000 without a full gut.

Puyallup homeowners are increasingly drawn to designs that balance modern function with Pacific Northwest warmth. Some of the most popular choices we install include:

Warm-toned quartz countertops with calacatta or marble-inspired veining
Shaker-style cabinetry in whites, soft grays, and warm wood tones
Matte black or brushed gold hardware for a sophisticated accent
Open shelving mixed with closed cabinetry for a curated look
Large single-basin sinks with touchless or pull-down faucets
Under-cabinet LED lighting for task lighting and ambiance
Waterfall edge islands with integrated seating

Want to see how these trends would look in your own kitchen? ReVision AI lets you snap a photo of your current space and instantly preview it in over 20 design styles, from Modern Farmhouse to Japandi to Contemporary.

Material Comparison: Choosing the Right Cabinetry

Cabinets eat up about 35-40% of a kitchen remodel budget, so this decision matters. Here’s how the main options compare:

Solid Wood (Maple, Cherry, Alder) The gold standard. Real wood cabinets with dovetail joints and soft-close hinges will last 30+ years with proper care. They can be refinished if styles change down the road. Expect to pay $20,000-$56,000 for a typical Puyallup kitchen (25-35 linear feet of cabinetry). I prefer maple for painted cabinets because it takes paint beautifully and resists warping in our humid Pacific Northwest climate.

Plywood Box with Solid Wood Doors This is the sweet spot for most of my clients. The cabinet boxes are built from 3/4-inch plywood (stronger and more moisture-resistant than particle board), and the doors and drawer fronts are solid wood. You get 90% of the quality at about 70% of the price. Typical cost: $13,000-$35,000.

Thermofoil / Rigid Thermofoil (RTF) A vinyl wrap over MDF. These are budget-friendly, easy to clean, and come in a wide variety of colors. They work well in rental properties and budget-conscious remodels. The downside: they can peel in high-heat areas (near the oven or dishwasher) and can’t be refinished. Typical cost: $8,000-$22,000.

Frameless (European-Style) Slab Cabinets Clean lines, no face frame, full-overlay doors. These give a very modern, contemporary look and maximize interior storage space. Popular with younger homeowners and anyone going for a minimalist design. Available in all the construction types above.

Countertop Options at a Glance

Your countertop choice affects both the look and daily function of your kitchen. Here’s a quick comparison of what we install most often:

Material	Cost per Sq Ft (Installed)	Durability	Maintenance	Best For
Quartz	$70-$190	Excellent	Wipe clean, no sealing	Most kitchens, families with kids
Granite	$60-$160	Excellent	Annual sealing	Homeowners who want natural stone character
Marble	$80-$240	Good (softer)	Regular sealing, stains easily	Baking stations, bathrooms, low-traffic areas
Butcher Block	$45-$120	Moderate	Oil regularly, sand out damage	Farmhouse style, prep sections, islands
Laminate	$20-$65	Moderate	Wipe clean	Budget remodels, rentals

For a deeper breakdown of each material, visit our countertop installation page.

Kitchen Flooring: What Works in the PNW

Flooring in a Pacific Northwest kitchen needs to handle moisture, mud tracked in from the rain, and heavy foot traffic. Here are the options I recommend:

Luxury Vinyl Plank (LVP): The most popular kitchen flooring I install right now. It’s 100% waterproof, comfortable underfoot, and comes in wood-look planks that are almost indistinguishable from real hardwood. Cost: $5-$13 per square foot installed. Lasts 15-25 years.

Porcelain Tile: Extremely durable and waterproof. Great for kitchens that open into mudrooms or back entries. Cost: $10-$24 per square foot installed. The downside is it’s cold and hard underfoot, though radiant heat mats can solve the comfort issue for an extra $7-$13 per square foot.

Hardwood: Beautiful, but I’m honest with my clients about the risks in a kitchen. Water around sinks and dishwashers can damage hardwood over time, especially in our damp climate. If you choose hardwood, go with a site-finished white oak and expect to refinish every 8-10 years. Cost: $13-$26 per square foot installed.

Kitchen Remodeling Cost Guide

Understanding costs upfront helps you plan confidently. Here’s what typical kitchen remodels cost in the Puyallup area based on the projects I’ve completed:

Budget Kitchen Refresh: $16,000-$40,000

Cabinet refacing or repainting
New countertops (laminate or entry-level quartz)
New backsplash
Updated hardware and fixtures
Keep existing layout and flooring

Mid-Range Full Remodel: $33,000-$88,000

New plywood-box cabinets with solid wood doors
Quartz or granite countertops
Tile backsplash
New LVP or tile flooring
Updated plumbing fixtures
New lighting (recessed + pendants)
Same layout or minor modifications

High-End Full Remodel: $72,000-$145,000+

Custom solid wood cabinetry
Premium quartz or natural stone countertops
Designer tile backsplash
Hardwood or large-format porcelain flooring
Layout changes (island addition, wall removal)
Built-in pantry and appliance garage
Under-cabinet and in-cabinet lighting
Premium fixtures throughout

Major Layout Change with Structural Work: $78,000-$160,000+ Everything in the high-end tier plus load-bearing wall removal, beam installation, significant plumbing rerouting, electrical panel upgrades, and potentially moving windows or exterior doors.

These ranges reflect Puyallup-area pricing for quality materials and professional installation. Every project is different, and I provide free, personalized estimates so you know exactly what your specific kitchen will cost.

PNW-Specific Challenges I Plan For

Remodeling in the Pacific Northwest isn’t the same as remodeling in Arizona or Texas. Here are a few things I account for on every kitchen project in this area:

Moisture and Ventilation: Our 40+ inches of annual rainfall and consistently high humidity mean moisture management matters inside your home. I always install proper range ventilation that exhausts to the outside (not just a recirculating fan). In kitchens with poor airflow, I’ll recommend adding a makeup air vent to prevent negative pressure issues.

Older Homes and Code Updates: Many Puyallup homes were built under older building codes. When we open up walls, we frequently find 2-wire electrical (no ground), undersized circuits, and galvanized plumbing. Bringing these up to current code is not optional; it’s required, and it’s the right thing to do. I build these potential costs into our estimates so there are no surprises.

Subfloor Condition: Homes from the 1970s-1990s often have 3/8-inch or 1/2-inch plywood subfloors that have softened over time, especially around dishwashers and sinks where slow leaks go unnoticed. We inspect and reinforce subfloors before installing new flooring to make sure everything is solid and level.

Lead Paint and Asbestos: Homes built before 1978 may have lead paint. Homes built before 1985 may have asbestos in vinyl flooring, popcorn ceilings, or pipe insulation. We test for both before demolition and follow EPA protocols for safe removal when needed.

Return on Investment: What a Kitchen Remodel Is Worth

Beyond the daily enjoyment of a kitchen you actually love using, a well-executed kitchen remodel is one of the best investments you can make in your home. It’s also one of the best financial decisions you can make as a homeowner.

According to the 2025 Remodeling Magazine Cost vs. Value Report for the Pacific Northwest:

A mid-range major kitchen remodel (average cost around $80,000 nationally, less in the Puyallup market) recoups approximately 49-75% of its cost at resale.
A minor kitchen remodel (cabinet refacing, new countertops, fixtures, and flooring) averaging around $27,000-$30,000 typically recoups 75-85% of its cost, making it one of the highest-ROI projects you can do.

Here’s what I tell my clients: the financial return matters, but it’s only part of the picture. If you plan to stay in your home for 5, 10, or 15 more years, the daily quality-of-life improvement is worth far more than the resale percentage. You’ll cook more. You’ll host more. You’ll actually enjoy being in your kitchen instead of dreading it.

And if you are selling soon, a modern, well-finished kitchen is the single most important factor in a buyer’s decision. Real estate agents in Pierce County will tell you the same thing. A dated kitchen with laminate counters and oak cabinets from 1993 can sit on the market for months. That same home with a freshly remodeled kitchen gets offers within weeks.

What to Expect During Your Free Consultation

When you call or fill out our contact form, here’s what happens next. I’ll schedule a time to meet you at your home, usually within a few days. During the consultation, which typically runs 45-60 minutes, we walk through your kitchen together while I take notes and measurements. I ask questions about how you use the space, what frustrates you, what you’ve seen that you like, and what your budget range looks like.

I don’t believe in high-pressure sales. I’m not going to show you a fancy presentation and try to close you on the spot. That’s not how I operate. You’ll get a written proposal within a week that includes a detailed scope of work, material specifications, a timeline, and a fixed price. Take your time reviewing it. Ask questions. Compare it to other bids if you’d like. When you’re ready, we’ll get your project on the schedule.

Most kitchen remodels book 4-6 weeks out from signed contract to start date, depending on the time of year and material lead times. Spring and summer are our busiest seasons, so if you’re planning a kitchen remodel for the warmer months, I’d recommend reaching out by February or March to lock in your spot.

Our Most Popular Kitchen Remodeling Service

Kitchen remodeling is our most requested service at Pacific Remodeling. I’ve earned that reputation by consistently delivering beautiful, functional kitchens on time and on budget. Whether you’re dreaming of a contemporary open-concept layout or a warm traditional kitchen with custom details, my team has the experience and skill to bring your vision to life.

I believe in doing every job as if I were working for the Lord, not just for a paycheck. That means honest pricing, quality materials, clean job sites, and a finished product I’d be proud to put in my own home.

Ready to get started? Contact us for your free kitchen remodeling estimate or call us at (253) 392-9266.

Bathroom Remodeling in Puyallup, WA

Create the bathroom retreat you've always wanted with expert renovations from Puyallup's trusted remodeling team.

WHAT'S INCLUDED
Our Bathroom Remodeling Services
Walk-In Showers

Custom-tiled walk-in showers with frameless glass, rain heads, body jets, and built-in niches. Curbless options for accessibility.

Bathtub Installation

Freestanding soaking tubs, alcove tubs, and tub-to-shower conversions professionally plumbed and installed.

Custom Tile Work

Expert Bathroom Renovations in Puyallup, WA

Your bathroom should be a place of comfort and relaxation, not a source of daily frustration. Whether it’s outdated tile from 1992, a cramped layout that barely fits one person, or a bathtub nobody has used in years, I can transform it into a space you’ll actually enjoy. I’ve renovated hundreds of bathrooms across Puyallup and Pierce County since 2018, from compact 40-square-foot guest baths to luxurious 120-square-foot master suites.

My team handles every aspect of the renovation in-house: demolition, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile, vanities, fixtures, and finish work. No subcontractors you’ve never met showing up at your door.

Walk-In Shower Conversions: Our Most Popular Request

If I had to pick the single most requested bathroom project we do, it’s converting an old bathtub into a walk-in shower. About 7 out of 10 bathroom remodels we complete include this conversion, and the reasons are simple: most families have at least one other tub in the house, the old tub-shower combo looks dated, and a walk-in shower makes the bathroom feel twice as large.

Here’s what goes into a proper tub-to-shower conversion:

Demolition and Plumbing Reconfiguration: We remove the tub, reroute the drain (tub drains and shower drains are in different locations), and adjust the supply lines and valve placement. If the existing plumbing is galvanized pipe, I’ll recommend upgrading to PEX while the walls are open. It adds $1,000-$2,400 to the project, but it prevents problems down the road.

Subfloor Repair and Slope: The shower floor needs to slope toward the drain at 1/4 inch per foot. We build a proper mortar bed or install a pre-sloped shower pan (Schluter KERDI is our go-to system). This step is non-negotiable because a flat shower floor means standing water and eventually mold.

Waterproofing: This is where bathrooms fail. I’ve torn out 5-year-old showers that were leaking into the subfloor because the original contractor skipped proper waterproofing. We use a full Schluter KERDI membrane system or equivalent on every shower, floor to ceiling. No exceptions. The waterproofing alone adds about $1,600-$3,200 to the project, and it’s worth every penny.

Tile Installation: Most clients choose large-format porcelain tile (12x24 or 24x48) for shower walls because it minimizes grout lines and looks clean. The shower floor typically gets a smaller mosaic tile (2x2 or hexagon) for slip resistance. We install built-in niches for shampoo and soap, usually 12”x24” or larger.

Glass Enclosure: A frameless glass door and panel opens up the bathroom visually and lets the tile work show. We custom-measure after tile is complete and the glass typically arrives within 7-10 days. Cost for a standard frameless enclosure runs $1,600-$4,000 depending on size and configuration.

Total Cost for a Tub-to-Shower Conversion: $10,000-$29,000 depending on size, tile selection, and fixture choices.

Bathroom Remodeling Services

Master Bathroom Suites: Full master bathroom renovations with dual vanities, freestanding soaking tubs, walk-in showers with multiple heads, heated floors, and custom storage solutions. These projects typically run $45,000-$105,000 and take 5-8 weeks.

Guest and Hall Bathrooms: Efficient renovations that maximize space and update the look with modern finishes. New vanity, tile surround, fixtures, and flooring. A typical hall bath remodel runs $16,000-$35,000 and takes 2-3 weeks.

Powder Rooms / Half Baths: New vanity, toilet, flooring, paint, mirror, and lighting. These small projects pack a big visual punch and typically cost $6,500-$16,000.

Bathroom Remodel Cost Ranges for the Puyallup Area

I believe in upfront pricing. Here’s what bathrooms actually cost in our market:

Project Type	Typical Cost Range	Timeline
Half bath / powder room update	$6,500 - $16,000	1-2 weeks
Standard tub-to-shower conversion	$10,000 - $29,000	2-3 weeks
Guest / hall bath full remodel	$16,000 - $35,000	2-3 weeks
Mid-range master bath remodel	$33,000 - $72,000	4-6 weeks
High-end master bath with layout change	$59,000 - $105,000+	6-8 weeks

These numbers include materials, labor, plumbing, electrical, and all finish work. Permits are additional when required (typically $250-$800 through the City of Puyallup).

Popular Bathroom Styles and Trends for 2026

Here’s what I’m seeing Puyallup homeowners choose right now:

Large-format porcelain tile (24x48” or larger) for a clean, modern look with minimal grout
Curbless walk-in showers for accessibility and a sleek aesthetic
Floating vanities that create visual space in smaller bathrooms, typically 30-36 inches tall
Matte black fixtures paired with white tile for high contrast
Linear drains for a contemporary shower floor, positioned along the back wall
Heated tile floors at $7-$13 per square foot installed, a must-have in the Pacific Northwest
Backlit mirrors replacing traditional medicine cabinets
Natural stone accent walls (marble-look porcelain) inside the shower
Warm wood-tone vanities replacing the all-white look that dominated the last decade

The biggest shift I’ve noticed over the past two years is away from the stark, all-white “spa bathroom” trend and toward warmer tones. Cream tiles, warm gray grout, wood-tone vanities, and brushed gold or brass fixtures are showing up in about half of my current projects.

Your Bathroom Remodel: Step by Step

Here’s exactly what to expect when you work with Pacific Remodeling:

Free consultation - I visit your home, discuss your vision, take measurements, and talk about materials and budget. This usually takes 45-60 minutes.
Design and proposal - Within a week, you’ll receive a detailed, fixed-price proposal with material selections, a scope of work, and a project timeline. No vague estimates or “we’ll figure it out as we go.”
Material selection - I’ll guide you through selecting tile, vanity, fixtures, countertops, and hardware. We visit showrooms together if needed.
Demolition and prep - Careful removal of existing materials with protection of surrounding floors and walls. Dust barriers go up on day one.
Plumbing and electrical - All rough-in work completed and inspected before we close up walls. This is when we upgrade old galvanized pipe, add GFCI outlets, and install exhaust fan ducting.
Waterproofing - Full membrane waterproofing system installed in all wet areas. This step gets inspected before any tile goes on.
Tile and finishes - Expert tile installation on floors, walls, and shower surfaces. Vanity mounting, fixture setting, mirror and accessory installation.
Final walkthrough - I walk through the finished bathroom with you and check every detail. If anything isn’t right, we fix it before we call the project complete.
Accessibility and Aging-in-Place Bathroom Design

I get more calls every year from homeowners who want to renovate their bathroom for long-term accessibility, either for themselves, a parent, or just smart planning for the future. These modifications don’t have to look institutional. Modern accessible design can be beautiful.

Curbless (Zero-Threshold) Showers: The shower floor is flush with the bathroom floor, which eliminates the tripping hazard of stepping over a curb. We achieve this by recessing the shower pan into the subfloor and using a linear drain at the shower entrance. This works in most homes, though older homes with limited joist depth may need a slight ramp instead.

Grab Bars and Blocking: We install solid wood blocking (2x6 or 3/4” plywood) behind the drywall in strategic locations so grab bars can be mounted securely at any time, now or years from now. The blocking is invisible once the walls are finished.

Comfort-Height Toilets: Standard toilet height is 15 inches. Comfort-height models sit at 17-19 inches, making it much easier to sit down and stand up. There’s no cost difference, so I recommend them on every project.

Wider Doorways: If the existing bathroom door is a standard 24-inch or 28-inch opening, we can widen it to 32 or 36 inches to accommodate a wheelchair or walker. This typically costs $500-$1,300 including new framing and trim.

Non-Slip Flooring: Small-format tile with more grout lines provides better traction on wet surfaces. We also recommend textured porcelain tile for shower floors.

Handheld Shower Heads on Slide Bars: These adjust from sitting to standing height and cost the same as a fixed shower head. I install them as a default on most projects.

Bathroom Remodel Return on Investment

A mid-range bathroom remodel in the Pacific Northwest typically recoups 60-70% of its cost at resale, according to the 2025 Remodeling Magazine Cost vs. Value Report. A bathroom addition (adding a new bathroom where one didn’t exist) can recoup even more because it changes the bedroom-to-bathroom ratio, which directly affects home value.

But here’s the real math I walk clients through: if you plan to live in your home for another 10 years and you use your bathroom twice a day, that’s over 7,000 uses. A $33,000 bathroom remodel works out to about $4.50 per use over that period. For a space that’s comfortable, beautiful, and works the way you need it to, that’s a pretty good deal.

PNW-Specific Bathroom Concerns

Ventilation: In our climate, bathroom ventilation isn’t optional. I install properly sized exhaust fans (minimum 80 CFM, 110+ CFM for larger bathrooms) ducted to the exterior on every project. Many older Puyallup homes have exhaust fans that vent into the attic, which is a mold disaster waiting to happen. We correct this as part of the remodel.

Moisture-Resistant Materials: We use moisture-resistant (green board) or cement board drywall in all bathroom areas and full waterproofing membranes in wet zones. Standard drywall has no place in a Pacific Northwest bathroom.

Mold Prevention: Proper waterproofing, adequate ventilation, and sealed grout lines are your three lines of defense against mold. I’ve seen the damage that happens when any one of these is skipped, and I won’t cut corners on any of them.

Older Home Surprises: Many Puyallup homes built before 1990 have original cast iron drain pipes, undersized venting, or subfloors weakened by decades of slow moisture exposure. When we open up a bathroom for remodeling, we inspect everything and bring it up to current code. This is especially common in the 1970s and 1980s ramblers that make up a large portion of the Puyallup housing market. I build potential remediation costs into our estimates so you’re not caught off guard.

What Sets Pacific Remodeling Apart

We Do the Work Ourselves. I don’t farm out your bathroom to a crew I’ve never worked with. My team handles every phase of the project, from the first swing of the demolition hammer to the final caulk line around your new tub.

Fixed-Price Proposals. You’ll know the total cost before we start. I don’t give vague estimates or charge by the hour. The price in your proposal is the price you pay, unless you decide to make changes during the project.

Communication. I keep you updated throughout the project with texts, photos, and in-person check-ins. If there’s a delay, you’ll know about it the same day, not a week later. If we find something unexpected behind a wall, I’ll show you, explain your options, and get your approval before moving forward.

Clean Job Sites. My crew cleans up at the end of every work day. Dust barriers go up on day one and stay up until the project is finished. Your home is your home, and we treat it that way.

Warranty and Follow-Up. We stand behind our work. If something isn’t right after we finish, call me and I’ll make it right. That’s not a slogan. It’s how my grandfather ran his business, how my father ran his, and how I run mine. Every piece of work that leaves our hands should be something I’d be proud to show anyone.

Why Pacific Remodeling for Your Bathroom

I approach every project the way I’d want someone to approach work in my own home. That means showing up on time, communicating clearly, keeping a clean job site, and delivering a result that lasts. My grandfather was a carpenter. My father was a carpenter. I’ve been in this trade for over 20 years, and the principle that guides my work hasn’t changed: do it right, treat people fairly, and stand behind your work.

PREMIUM SURFACES
Countertop Installation in Puyallup, WA

Professional installation of granite, quartz, marble, and solid surface countertops with precision templating and flawless results.

WHAT'S INCLUDED
Our Countertop Installation Services
Quartz Countertops

Non-porous engineered stone that resists stains, scratches, and heat without sealing. Wide range of colors and patterns.

Granite Countertops

Natural stone with unique slab patterns. Extremely hard and heat-resistant when properly sealed.

Marble Countertops

Classic veining and luminous surface ideal for bathroom vanities, baking stations, and formal kitchens.

Butcher Block

Warm, natural hardwood surfaces suited to farmhouse and transitional kitchen designs.

Professional Countertop Installation

New countertops can completely transform the look and feel of your kitchen or bathroom. I’ve installed thousands of square feet of countertops across Puyallup and Pierce County, and I can tell you this: no single upgrade changes a room faster than replacing the counters. Pacific Remodeling handles everything from material selection to precision fabrication and flawless installation.

Whether you’re replacing worn-out laminate in a kitchen remodel or upgrading a bathroom vanity top, we’ll walk you through every option and help you choose what fits your space, your lifestyle, and your budget.

Our Process: From Selection to Installation

Here’s exactly how a countertop project works with Pacific Remodeling:

In-home consultation (Day 1) - I measure your space, discuss material options, review edge profiles (eased, beveled, bullnose, waterfall), and provide a written estimate. This visit takes about 30-45 minutes.
Slab selection (Week 1) - For natural stone and many quartz options, we visit the slab yard together so you can see the full slab and pick the exact piece for your home. Colors and veining vary from slab to slab, so seeing them in person matters.
Digital templating (After cabinets are set) - A fabricator visits your home with laser-guided measuring equipment and captures exact dimensions, including sink cutouts, faucet holes, cooktop openings, and backsplash returns. This digital template is accurate to within 1/16 of an inch.
Fabrication (5-7 business days) - Slabs are cut, polished, and edge-finished based on your approved template. Sink cutouts are made, and seam locations are planned to minimize visibility.
Installation (1 day) - Countertops are delivered, set on the cabinets, leveled, seamed with color-matched epoxy, and sealed (if natural stone). Sinks and faucets are reconnected the same day so you have a working kitchen or bathroom by evening.

Total timeline from consultation to completed installation: 2-3 weeks for a straightforward replacement. 5-7 weeks if the countertops are part of a larger kitchen or bathroom remodel.

Material Comparison: Picking the Right Countertop

This is the question I answer more than any other. Here’s an honest breakdown of each material, with real numbers from our market.

Quartz (Engineered Stone)

Quartz is our most popular countertop material. About 60% of the countertops we install are quartz.

Cost: $70-$190 per square foot installed (a typical 40 sq ft kitchen runs $2,800-$7,600)
Pros: Non-porous, never needs sealing, extremely consistent color and pattern, resists stains and scratches, wide range of styles from solid colors to natural stone look-alikes
Cons: Not heat-proof (trivets are required for hot pans), can discolor in direct sunlight over time (not ideal for outdoor kitchens), manufactured appearance may not appeal to those who want “real” stone
Best for: Busy family kitchens, bathrooms, anyone who wants low maintenance
Popular brands: Cambria, Caesarstone, Silestone, MSI

The calacatta-inspired quartz with warm white backgrounds and soft gray veining is the number one seller in Puyallup right now.

Granite (Natural Stone)

Granite was king for 20 years and still has a loyal following for good reason.

Cost: $60-$160 per square foot installed (a typical 40 sq ft kitchen runs $2,400-$6,400)
Pros: Natural and unique (no two slabs are identical), extremely hard, heat-resistant (you can set a hot pan on it), adds undeniable character to a kitchen
Cons: Requires annual sealing to prevent staining, some colors are more porous than others (lighter granites stain more easily), natural fissures and pits are normal but bother some people
Best for: Homeowners who value natural materials, high-heat cooking areas, anyone who wants a one-of-a-kind look
Popular colors in our area: White Ice, Alaska White, Steel Grey, Colonial White
Marble (Natural Stone)

Marble is beautiful. It’s also high-maintenance. I’m upfront about this with every client.

Cost: $80-$240 per square foot installed
Pros: Timeless, elegant veining, cool surface temperature (ideal for baking and pastry work), high-end look that nothing else replicates
Cons: Soft stone that scratches and etches easily (lemon juice, wine, and tomato sauce will etch the surface), requires frequent sealing, stains more easily than granite or quartz, highest maintenance of any countertop material
Best for: Bathroom vanities, dedicated baking stations, formal kitchens with careful owners, decorative surfaces
My honest advice: I love marble. I also tell clients to consider it carefully for a primary kitchen work surface. If you’re comfortable with a “living finish” that develops character over time, marble is stunning. If water rings and knife marks will stress you out, go with a marble-look quartz instead.
Butcher Block (Hardwood)

Warm, natural, and perfect for certain applications.

Cost: $45-$120 per square foot installed
Pros: Warm, inviting look, can be sanded and refinished when damaged, naturally antimicrobial, softer on dropped dishes and glasses, perfect for farmhouse and transitional kitchens
Cons: Requires regular oiling (monthly for the first year, then every 2-3 months), can be damaged by standing water, not heat-resistant, scratches and dents over time (though many people consider this “character”)
Best for: Island tops, prep areas, farmhouse-style kitchens, breakfast bars
Wood options: Maple (most popular), walnut (darker, more expensive), white oak, cherry

In our Pacific Northwest climate, I always recommend a marine-grade penetrating oil finish for butcher block because the humidity levels here are higher than in drier regions.

Laminate

Don’t overlook laminate. Modern laminate has come a long way from the flat, fake-looking surfaces of the past.

Cost: $20-$65 per square foot installed
Pros: Most affordable option, huge variety of colors and patterns (including convincing stone and wood looks), no sealing required, easy to clean
Cons: Can chip or scratch, not heat-resistant, visible seams, shorter lifespan (10-15 years vs. 25+ for stone), can’t be repaired easily
Best for: Budget remodels, rental properties, laundry rooms, secondary prep areas
Care and Maintenance Tips by Material

Quartz: Wipe down daily with a damp cloth and mild dish soap. Avoid harsh chemicals like bleach or abrasive cleaners. Always use trivets for hot pans. That’s it.

Granite: Clean with a pH-neutral stone cleaner or mild dish soap. Seal once per year with a quality impregnating sealer (takes about 15 minutes). Blot spills quickly, especially acidic liquids like wine or citrus juice.

Marble: Clean with a pH-neutral stone cleaner only, never vinegar or citrus-based products. Seal every 3-6 months. Use coasters and trivets religiously. Accept that etching will happen with normal use and learn to love the patina, or plan on professional honing every few years.

Butcher Block: Oil with food-safe mineral oil or a cutting board oil monthly for the first year, then every 2-3 months. Wipe up standing water immediately. Sand out deep scratches or stains with 220-grit sandpaper and re-oil.

Laminate: Wipe with a damp cloth and mild soap. Avoid abrasive scrubbers. Use cutting boards and trivets. Keep seams dry to prevent swelling.

Why the Right Installer Matters

A $5,000 slab of quartz is only as good as the installation underneath it. I’ve seen countertops crack because cabinets weren’t level, seams that looked like zipper lines because the fabricator rushed, and sink cutouts that leaked because the undermount clips were installed wrong. My team levels every cabinet run before we template, we plan seam locations to fall in low-visibility areas, and we test every sink connection before we leave.
